items.text: How do I enquire about a Jetking franchise? Franchise enquiries go through a dedicated team. Submitting the franchise enquiry form starts a conversation about territory availability, the operating model and what partnership involves.
items.title: Jetking FAQ

items.text: What will I learn? Deploying secure, robust applications on AWS, covering AWS Services, Management Tools, Databases and Security, and Troubleshooting, focused on the IMS Track across Foundation, Associate, and Architect levels.
items.title: AWS Solution Specialist — FAQ

items.text: Does AWS Solution Architect require coding? No, AWS Solution Architect roles typically do not require extensive coding, though familiarity with scripting languages like Python and basic programming concepts can be beneficial for some tasks.
items.title: AWS Solution Specialist — FAQ

items.text: How will this course enhance my career prospects? AWS dominates the cloud market, creating high demand. The IMS Track offers roles like Help Desk Support-Cloud Services, Cloud Associate L1, and AWS Cloud NOC Support/Executive L1.
items.title: AWS Solution Specialist — FAQ

items.text: What are the entry requirements? Any graduate or 10+2 student wanting a cloud career can enroll. Knowledge of hardware, networking and servers is required; others can take Jetking's IoT Bridge Course first.
items.title: AWS Solution Specialist — FAQ

items.text: How to become an AWS solution architect? Develop strong understanding of AWS services, obtain certifications, gain hands-on project experience, stay updated with industry trends, network with professionals, and seek mentorship.
items.title: AWS Solution Specialist — FAQ

items.text: What is the cost of AWS certification? The cost varies depending on the specific certification exam, with prices typically ranging from Rs.6,000 to Rs.30,000 in Indian rupees.
items.title: AWS Solution Specialist — FAQ

items.text: What is the eligibility criteria for the Jetking BCA degree program? Candidates must have completed 10+2 from a recognized board. Mathematics or Computer Science is preferred, but the curriculum builds foundations from scratch, making it accessible to students from various streams.
items.title: BCA in Cloud Computing & Cyber Security — FAQ

items.text: Can I pursue a BCA if I didn't have Mathematics in my 12th grade? Yes. Many specialization tracks include Fundamentals of Mathematics in the early semesters to ensure all students reach the required proficiency.
items.title: BCA in Cloud Computing & Cyber Security — FAQ

items.text: How does Jetking's BCA differ from a traditional BCA? Jetking integrates curriculum mapped with global certifications (Microsoft, AWS, Red Hat), and its SmartLab approach emphasizes 60-70% practical hands-on learning versus purely academic programs.
items.title: BCA in Cloud Computing & Cyber Security — FAQ

items.text: Does Jetking provide placement guarantee for BCA students? Yes. Jetking provides 100% placement guarantee including 360-degree support: resume building, mock interviews with industry experts, and access to placement partners.
items.title: BCA in Cloud Computing & Cyber Security — FAQ

items.text: What is the duration and format of the course? The BCA is a 3-year, 6-semester full-time degree program, UGC-approved, delivered through offline or hybrid mode.
items.title: BCA in Cloud Computing & Cyber Security — FAQ

items.text: Are there flexible payment options for the course fees? Yes. Jetking offers flexible fee structures including one-time payments and easy installment modes.

items.text: What is a Data Analyst and what does a Data Analyst do? A Data Analyst collects, cleans, and analyzes data to help businesses make better decisions using tools like Excel, SQL, Power BI, Python, and Tableau to create reports and dashboards.

items.text: What skills are required to become a Data Analyst? You need skills in data analysis, statistics, Excel, SQL, Python, data visualization tools like Power BI or Tableau, and the ability to interpret business data.

items.text: What is ethical hacker salary? The typical monthly salary for an Ethical Hacker in India is around Rs.218,000, with additional cash compensation averaging Rs.168,000, ranging from Rs.24,167 to Rs.435,000.
items.title: Ethical Hacking Specialist — FAQ

items.text: Is Ethical Hacking legal? Yes, Ethical Hacking is legal when conducted with proper authorization. Ethical hackers must obtain permission from the system owner before any security testing or assessment.
items.title: Ethical Hacking Specialist — FAQ

items.text: Is hands-on experience provided in Ethical Hacking courses? Yes, Jetking Ethical Hacking courses include hands-on labs and practical exercises crucial for developing skills to identify and exploit vulnerabilities in real-world scenarios.
items.title: Ethical Hacking Specialist — FAQ

items.text: Which certifications should I pursue alongside MCA? AWS Certified Solutions Architect, Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900), Google Associate Cloud Engineer, Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH), CompTIA Security+, and CISSP.

items.text: What is the Microsoft Server MCTS certification? MCTS validates your skills in a specific Microsoft technology such as Windows Server, demonstrating your ability to install, configure, and troubleshoot in a Microsoft server environment.
items.title: Microsoft Server Technology Specialist — FAQ

items.text: What are the prerequisites for enrolling in the Microsoft Server MCTS course? Basic knowledge of computer hardware, networking, and Windows operating systems is recommended. Some experience in IT or a related field can also be beneficial.
items.title: Microsoft Server Technology Specialist — FAQ

items.text: Who should take the Microsoft Server MCTS course? Ideal for IT professionals, Microsoft system administrators, and anyone seeking to enhance skills in managing Microsoft server environments or pursue advanced certifications.

items.text: Why choose Jetking for the Microsoft Server course? Immersive learning with interactive material, experienced mentors, skilled evaluators, real-world expert-designed projects, and career services including resume development and interview preparation.
items.title: Microsoft Server Technology Specialist — FAQ

items.text: What is essential networking? Connecting computers and devices to share resources like internet, files, printers and services, covering IP addressing, DNS, routing, switching and network security for communication and data transfer.
items.title: Networking Essentials Specialist — FAQ

items.text: What are the 3 types of networking? LAN connects devices within a limited area; WAN covers broad areas linking multiple LANs over long distances; MAN spans a city or large campus between LAN and WAN scale.
items.title: Networking Essentials Specialist — FAQ

items.text: What is the importance of this course? Computer Hardware and Networking is a fast-growing occupation; this PC Hardware Support course prepares students to maintain desktops in terms of hardware, operating system and applications.
items.title: PC Hardware Support — FAQ

items.text: What is a hardware course? A program focused on the physical components of computers and electronic devices, how they work, how to assemble and disassemble them, and how to troubleshoot hardware-related issues.
items.title: PC Hardware Support — FAQ

items.text: Which computer hardware course is best? It depends on your goals, but courses like CompTIA A+, Cisco CCNA, or courses from manufacturers such as Microsoft, Dell or HP are highly regarded.
items.title: PC Hardware Support — FAQ

items.text: What is this course about? Powered by Red Hat, this course provides all the training required to become a Red Hat Certified System Administrator (RHCSA) and pass the EX200 exam.
items.title: Red Hat Professional (RHCSA) — FAQ

items.text: What will I learn in Red Hat course (RHCSA)? You will learn Red Hat System Administration I (RH124) and II (RH134), starting with fundamentals of shell commands, creating and modifying users, changing passwords and more.
items.title: Red Hat Professional (RHCSA) — FAQ

items.text: How will this Linux certified course enhance my career prospects? It opens many job opportunities for a Linux systems administrator in reputed companies, with higher positions and strong career growth as you gain experience.
items.title: Red Hat Professional (RHCSA) — FAQ

items.text: Who is the Red Hat Linux course suitable for? Individuals interested in becoming proficient Linux system administrators, whether beginners or experienced professionals seeking formal recognition of their skills.
items.title: Red Hat Professional (RHCSA) — FAQ

items.text: What is CCNA (Cisco Certified Network Associate)? CCNA is a globally recognized IT certification from Cisco for those new to networking, validating skills to understand, configure, operate and troubleshoot medium-level switched and routed networks.
items.title: Routing & Switching Administrator (CCNA) — FAQ

items.text: What is routing and switching? Routing directs data packets between networks based on destination IP addresses; switching forwards packets within a single network based on device MAC addresses for efficient communication.
items.title: Routing & Switching Administrator (CCNA) — FAQ

items.text: What is the role of a routing and switching job? Configuring, managing, and troubleshooting network routers and switches, designing topologies, optimizing performance, implementing security, and resolving connectivity issues.
items.title: Routing & Switching Administrator (CCNA) — FAQ

items.text: Frequently asked questions — Routing & Switching Administrator (CCNA) — 2 Months | Jetking What is CCNA (Cisco Certified Network Associate)?. CCNA is a globally recognized IT certification from Cisco for those new to networking, validating skills to understand, configure, operate and troubleshoot medium-level switched and routed networks.. What will I learn?. Managing Cisco switches and routers, infrastructure security commands, WAN design and implementation, troubleshooting, network fundamentals, IP addressing, LAN switching, and routing technologies.. What is routing and switching?. Routing directs data packets between networks based on destination IP addresses; switching forwards packets within a single network based on device MAC addresses for efficient communication.. What are the entry requirements?. Technical graduates (BE/BSc IT) need no prior knowledge. Non-technical graduates or 10+2 students can pursue the course alongside Jetking's Networking Essentials Module.. What is the role of a routing and switching job?. Configuring, managing, and troubleshooting network routers and switches, designing topologies, optimizing performance, implementing security, and resolving connectivity issues.. items.text: BCA in Cloud Computing & Cyber Security Programme: BCA in Cloud Computing & Cyber Security. Level: degree. Duration: 3 years. Eligibility: Pass in 10+2 from any recognised board (State / CBSE / ICSE / NIOS / IB / IGCSE). Students appearing for 10+2 may also apply. No entrance test. A UGC-approved bachelor degree specialising in cloud architecture and cyber security, with hands-on labs and paid internships. Students build expertise in cloud platforms, information security, cryptography and digital forensics. What you can do after it: Enter roles such as Cloud Administrator, SOC Analyst or Network Security Specialist; Design and secure cloud infrastructure on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud; Graduate with a recognised BCA degree stacked with global certifications. Modules covered: Programming in C, C++, OOP and data structures; Networking, inter-networking (Cisco) and server OS (Windows / Linux); Enterprise Linux (RHCSA), Azure and AWS cloud administration; Ethical hacking (CEH), cyber laws and digital forensics (CHFI); Penetration testing, Splunk security and capstone project. Industry certifications: AWS, Microsoft Azure, CEH, CHFI, Red Hat (RHCSA), Cisco.

items.text: What is the profile of a Jetking Franchisee? Question: What is the profile of a Jetking Franchisee? items.text: Customer experience is paramount — Customer experience is paramount Customer experience is paramount Sunday, May 28, 2023 For online food aggregator platforms to be successful in India there has to be an algorithm to interpret customer feedback, monitor trends and make predictions, minimising risk and allowing for experimentation. By adopting technology, you’re embracing the idea of being able to try things and gather data. Customer autonomy and choice is paramount in today’s food tech scene. Food tech is here to stay. The double digit growth year on year is a testament to that. But due to overlapping of similar models, it will boil down to the survival of only the profitable. At present the cash strapped players have decided to outdo competition by offering heavy discounts. But pricing by itself may not be a deciding factor. It will play a crucial role, especially for those who tend to use these platforms more often than others, but in the long run it is not a sustainable business model. Below are some tips that can keep you smartphone and information safe: Set up a security lock Privacy is always important to us and it is advised use either a pattern, pin or password lock to prevent unwanted access to your phone. Above all, never share your password, security key lock for your smartphone with anyone. items.text: 4 Key Aspects Of ERP Implementation — 4 Key Aspects Of ERP Implementation 4 Key Aspects Of ERP Implementation Sunday, May 28, 2023 Choosing the right ERP system from the zillions available in the market can be confusing. Here are four aspects that you should consider to find the perfect match of ERP system for your organisation. 1. Determine: You understand your business better than anyone. An ERP solution should be able to address the organization’s needs across all parts of the business like marketing, finance and HR- whether it is reaching out to the target audience, big data and analytics and end-to-end employee intranet for employee communication. The same should help you integration of multiple software for easier business intelligence. 2. Evaluate: While many companies choose a solution based on brand name it is always advisable to choose a solution on the basis of your organization’s needs and technical capabilities. Also, evaluate the cost of changing to a new ERP software from the previous method in place. While selecting the ERP, the technology requirement must be looked at in a 60/30/10 format – 60% of what is needed today, 30% for near future and 10% for long-term. items.text: Hardware with software — Hardware with software Hardware with software Sunday, May 28, 2023 India has recently surpassed US as the largest consumer market of smartphones. With the rising number of the digital native generation consumers this demand is only poised to grow further. Hardware plays a major role for us to stay connected with one another. High end laptops, HD cable and iPhones are found even in the most unsuspected parts of India. The fact that market researchers do not check mobile phones while collecting information about SEC data due to their ubiquitous presence bears testament to this. We go to the fanciest malls to purchase these gadgets, but if anything goes wrong we visit the local handyman. But on hearing the price of repair, very often one is often confused between repairing and simply buying a new device. A similar thought has been reflected in the career choices students are make when it comes to IT. There is an increase in the number of students wanting to learn app development and a drop in the number of students wanting to learn hardware, which is essentially the backbone of IT. items.text: Indispensable Engineers — Indispensable Engineers Indispensable Engineers Sunday, May 28, 2023 Virtual engineers, automation engineers or robotic engineers design, programme, simulate and test automated machinery and processes in order to complete exact tasks. Automation engineers are responsible for design specifications and other detailed documentation of their creations. Automation is a field that involves creating and applying technologies that control or monitor production and delivery. There are automation opportunities in both product and service oriented industries. Two professional associations, the International Society of Automation and the Automation Federation, are involved in promoting and supporting the field of automation. The duties of an automation engineer include designing, programming, simulating and testing automated machinery or processes that are intended to complete precise tasks — for example, robots used in packaging, food processing or vehicle manufacturing. Automation engineers work with automated machinery from concept to prototype and are responsible for providing detailed documentation including design specifications that enable the production or application of their products. items.text: Need more integrated partnership — Need more integrated partnership Need more integrated partnership Sunday, May 28, 2023 Finance Minister Arun Jaitley announced several proposals in the ‘Make in India’ initiative. The creation of a Higher Education Funding Agency (HEFA) with Rs 1,000 crore for the improvement of infrastructure in higher education institutions is a decision in the right direction. Whereas in the case of skill development, the government has announced 1,500 multiskill training institutes across the country with a recognized board for certification purposes. Hopefully, this will enhance the recognition of formally skilled alumni and youth will be more widely accepted for employment in public and private sector. Also, to incentivize the employers to recruit unemployed persons and bring into the books the informal employees to ensure new jobs are created in the formal sector. The Centre’s decision to pay the Employee Pension Scheme contribution of 8.33 per cent for all new employees enrolling in EPFO for the first three years of their employment is also commendable. ‘Make in India’ is a workable solution for employment and economic growth in the long term. Your college may get top organisations for campus placements. However, at the end of the day, top organisations may end up picking just the toppers! And what’s worse? You’re not one of them! This leaves you worried that organisations outside may also misjudge you that if you haven’t been placed by organisations on campus then why would they hire you? You may then choose to just take up a support job rather than being unemployed. But a job is not always a matter of chance. You can actively decide where you want to be and make it happen. Here’s how: Look for an internship: You can look for an internship paid or unpaid in the area of your liking. This not only gets you a professional experience but you progress and perform you stand a chance of becoming a permanent employee there! Earn additional certifications: So if you want your CV to be noticed and picked up amongst the thousands available online, you need to acquire relevant certifications in your field. For example, you could take up a certification in ethical hacking in order to get a job as a security analyst or a course in network analyst. Tuesday, May 16, 2023 Before we begin to manage time, we must understand what time is. A dictionary defines time as “the point or period at which things occur.” In simple words, time is when stuff happens. In the real world there are two types of time: “clock time” and “real time.” In clock time, there are 60 seconds in a minute, 60 minutes in an hour, 24 hours in a day and 365 days in a year. And what’s interesting to note here is that all time passes in the same way. When somebody turns 60, they are accurately 60 years old, no more or no less. In real time, all time is proportional. Now, your real time flies or drags entirely depend on what you’re doing. Two hours waiting for a Bus at the bus station feel like 10 years, you see your watch hundred times in between, fiddle around with your phone, read a book, listen to music on your music player and a lot of things you do, just to pass your two hours of waiting time. And yet you meet your cousin after 5 years and you feel that he has grown up in only two hours. Which time describes the world in which you really live, real time or clock time? items.text: Cyber security or cloud computing: how to tell which one suits you — The shape of the work Cloud engineering is constructive. You are building, automating and improving systems, and the feedback loop is that something works better than it did. Security is investigative and adversarial. You are looking for what is wrong, often under time pressure, and the feedback loop is that nothing bad happened. People who enjoy finishing things tend to prefer cloud. People who enjoy finding things tend to prefer security.
items.title: Cyber security or cloud computing: how to tell which one suits you — The shape of the work

items.text: Cyber security or cloud computing: how to tell which one suits you — What both require Solid networking fundamentals — non-negotiable for either. Comfort with Linux. Willingness to keep learning after the certification is signed
items.title: Cyber security or cloud computing: how to tell which one suits you — What both require

items.text: Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers — Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers Career changers consistently underestimate how much of their existing experience counts. A look at what transfers, what does not, and how to sequence the change. The anxiety most career changers bring is that they are starting from zero. In practice, they are not — but the things that transfer are rarely the things they expect.
items.title: Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers — Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers

items.text: Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers — What transfers Working professionally: meeting deadlines, escalating clearly, handling a difficult stakeholder. Domain knowledge — a banking background is a genuine advantage in BFSI security roles. Judgement about what matters, which is the hardest thing to teach a fresh graduate
items.title: Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers — What transfers

items.text: Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers — What does not Technical fundamentals have to be built properly. There is no shortcut here, and attempting one produces the most common failure mode: a candidate who can operate a tool but cannot diagnose why it stopped working.
items.title: Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers — What does not

items.text: Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers — Sequencing the change Most successful changers do not resign first. Evening or weekend batches, then a period of overlap, then the move. It takes longer and it works more often.
items.title: Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers — Sequencing the change

items.text: Seven questions parents should ask any IT training institute — Seven questions parents should ask any IT training institute A checklist for families evaluating technical training — the questions that separate a substantive programme from a well-marketed one. Parents funding a technical programme are making a significant decision with limited technical context. These questions are designed to be answerable by any institute acting in good faith. What is the recognition status of the qualification, and who recognises it?. What proportion of the last completed batch was placed, and where?. What is the total cost, including certification and examination fees?. Who teaches, and what is their industry background?. What does placement support actually consist of — is it introductions, or is it training?. What happens if my child struggles partway through?. Can I speak to a recent graduate?
items.title: Seven questions parents should ask any IT training institute — Seven questions parents should ask any IT training institute

items.text: Seven questions parents should ask any IT training institute — On placement claims Ask for the denominator. A placement percentage is only meaningful alongside how many students it was calculated from and whether it counts students who did not complete the programme. A serious institute will answer all seven without hesitation. Reluctance on any of them is itself information.
items.title: Seven questions parents should ask any IT training institute — On placement claims

items.text: The DevOps skills employers are actually screening for — The DevOps skills employers are actually screening for Job descriptions list twenty tools. Interviews test about four things. Here is the gap, and what to prioritise. DevOps job descriptions have become inventories of every tool the team has ever touched. Interview processes are far narrower, and understanding that difference saves months of misdirected study.
items.title: The DevOps skills employers are actually screening for — The DevOps skills employers are actually screening for

items.text: The DevOps skills employers are actually screening for — What gets tested Can you debug a failing pipeline you did not write?. Do you understand what a container actually is, beyond the commands?. Can you reason about a production incident under questioning?. Do you write automation that someone else can maintain?
items.title: The DevOps skills employers are actually screening for — What gets tested

items.text: The DevOps skills employers are actually screening for — What rarely gets tested Tool-specific syntax recall. Interviewers assume documentation exists. Depth in one toolchain consistently beats shallow familiarity with six.

Overview CCNA (Cisco Certified Network Associate) is an information technology (IT) certification from Cisco.This is a globally recognised certification for those who are new or fresh in their networking career. This is a second level of certifaction one step above Cisco Certified Entry Networking Technician. Holding this certification states that the individual has the desired skills to understand, configure, operate & trouble shoot medium level switched and routed network. Jetking provides training on this certification track so that individuals who are keen to clear this certification can get trained by us. Some companies have made it mandatory to have these skills to be employed in the IT Network domain.

What will I learn? This course has been mapped to the CCNA (200-125) certification track of CISCO and deals with the following Topics 1. Managing Cisco Switches and Routers using IOS Commands 2. Cisco commands for managing Infrastructure Security, Infrastrucutre Services. 3. Design and implement Cisco WAN technologies 4. Troubleshooting Cisco Devices 5. Network Fundamentals 6. IP Addressing 7. Basic LAN Switching Technologies 8. Advanced LAN switching technologies 9. Working with CISCO devices 10. Basic & advanced routing technologies 11. Infrastructure Services 12. Infrastructure Security Infrastructure Management 13. Basic & advanced trouble shooting 14. WAN technologies

What is routing and switching? Routing and switching are fundamental functions in computer networking. Routing involves directing data packets between different networks based on their destination IP addresses, enabling communication between devices across different networks. Switching, on the other hand, involves forwarding data packets within a single network based on the MAC addresses of devices, allowing for efficient communication within the same network segment.

What is the role of a routing and switching job? The role of a routing and switching job involves configuring, managing, and troubleshooting network routers and switches to ensure efficient data transmission within a computer network. This includes designing network topologies, optimizing network performance, implementing security measures, and resolving connectivity issues.

How will this course enhance My career prospects? Companies are in need of certified networking professionals with excellent working knowledge of protocols like IP, EIGRP, Serial, Frame Relay, IP RIP, VLAN’s etc for installing, configuring, operating, maintaining, and troubleshooting LAN, WAN and other networks. This course will help you to gain all these skills. You also receive a Jetking Certification on these skills. Following are some Job roles that you can look to work with after this course 1. IT Network Administrator L1 2. Network Engineer L1 3. System & Network Support Engineer L1 4. LAN Support Engineer L1

What is essential networking? Essential networking involves connecting computers and other devices to share resources, such as internet access, files, printers, and services. It includes basic concepts like IP addressing, DNS, routing, switching, and network security to ensure communication and data transfer across devices within a network.

What are the entry requirements? The entry requirements typically include a basic understanding of computer systems, networking concepts, and sometimes a relevant educational background or previous experience in IT. Specific requirements may vary depending on the course or program.

What are the 3 types of networking? The three main types of networking are: 1. Local Area Network (LAN): A network that connects devices within a limited area, such as a home, school, or office building. 2. Wide Area Network (WAN): A network that covers a broad area, often connecting multiple LANs, typically over long distances, such as between cities or countries. 3. Metropolitan Area Network (MAN): A network that spans a city or large campus, providing connectivity within a larger geographic area than a LAN but smaller than a WAN.

20 Azure Interview Questions & Answers for 2025 20 Azure Interview Questions & Answers for 2025 Microsoft Azure continues to be a dominant force in cloud computing, making it essential for IT professionals to stay updated on the latest concepts. Whether you're preparing for a job interview or simply brushing up on your Azure knowledge, this blog covers 20 commonly asked Azure interview questions and their detailed answers for 2025. 1. What is Microsoft Azure? Microsoft Azure is a cloud computing platform and service offered by Microsoft that provides a range of solutions such as computing, storage, networking, and AI. It enables businesses to build, manage, and deploy applications across a global network of Microsoft-managed data centres.

20 Azure Interview Questions & Answers for 2025 Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is a managed Kubernetes container orchestration service that simplifies the deployment, management, and scaling of containerized applications. 7. What is Azure Functions? Azure Functions is a serverless compute service that allows users to execute small pieces of code in response to events, such as HTTP requests, database updates, or timers, without provisioning entire virtual machines. 8. What is Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)? Azure AD is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management (IAM) service that helps employees sign in and access resources securely. It supports multi-factor authentication, single sign-on (SSO), and identity protection.

20 Azure Interview Questions & Answers for 2025 Azure DevOps is a set of development tools and services that help with CI/CD, infrastructure automation, version control, and project tracking. It includes Azure Repos, Azure Pipelines, Azure Boards, and Azure Test Plans. 10. How does Azure Site Recovery work? Azure Site Recovery (ASR) ensures business continuity by replicating workloads to Azure. In case of outages, workloads can failover to Azure and later failback when the issue is resolved. 11. What is Azure Logic Apps? Azure Logic Apps is a cloud-based workflow service that helps automate and integrate business processes by connecting various services like Office 365, SAP, and Salesforce.

20 Azure Interview Questions & Answers for 2025 12. What is Azure Cosmos DB? Azure Cosmos DB is a globally distributed NoSQL database service designed for high availability, low latency, and automatic scaling. It supports multiple data models, including document, key-value, graph, and column-family. 13. What is Azure Load Balancer? Azure Load Balancer distributes incoming network traffic across multiple servers to ensure high availability and fault tolerance for applications. 14. What is Azure Monitor? Azure Monitor is a service that collects, analyzes, and visualizes telemetry data to improve application performance, security, and troubleshooting.

20 Azure Interview Questions & Answers for 2025 15. How does Azure Backup work? Azure Backup is a cloud-based backup solution that protects data by creating recovery points and storing them securely in Azure Recovery Services Vault. 16. What is Azure Virtual Network (VNet)? Azure Virtual Network (VNet) is a networking service that allows Azure resources to securely communicate with each other, the internet, or on-premises networks. 17. What is Azure Data Factory? Azure Data Factory is a cloud-based data integration service that enables data movement and transformation across various data stores. 18. What is Azure Sentinel? Azure Sentinel is a cloud-native SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) tool that uses AI for threat detection, investigation, and response.

20 Azure Interview Questions & Answers for 2025 19. What is Azure Traffic Manager? Azure Traffic Manager is a DNS-based traffic routing service that distributes user requests across different regions to optimize performance and availability. 20. What is Azure ExpressRoute? Azure ExpressRoute is a private connection service that enables secure, high-bandwidth connectivity between on-premises networks and Azure, bypassing the public internet. By preparing with these Azure interview questions, you can confidently demonstrate your expertise in cloud computing and stand out in job interviews. Azure continues to evolve, so staying updated with the latest services and best practices is crucial for career growth in cloud technology.

Evaluate: While many companies choose a solution based on brand name it is always advisable to choose a solution on the basis of your organization’s needs and technical capabilities. Also, evaluate the cost of changing to a new ERP software from the previous method in place. While selecting the ERP, the technology requirement must be looked at in a 60/30/10 format – 60% of what is needed today, 30% for near future and 10% for long-term. While investing in the right ERP software can reduce the future costs of human error, it is essential to evaluate the total costs. Beware of the hidden costs.

4 Key Aspects Of ERP Implementation 3. Develop: It is important to develop a realistic implementation plan to include all the activities from installing the software to ensuring that it is functional, tested and accepted by the users. 4. Measure: Adopting a new ERP software is a way to reduce costs, increase revenue, or scale for growth and hence you should estimate and measure benefits against these metrics to realize the potential benefits. Difference between AWS, Azure and GCP Difference between AWS, Azure and GCP 5 Key Difference between AWS, Azure and GCP In the past decade, there has been rapid growth in the cloud computing landscape, with Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform among the top players. Although each of the three has a reach of cloud-based services, some important differences will make or break your cloud strategy. We'll walk through five critical differences that will give you a clear choice between AWS, Azure, and GCP. Difference #1: Compute Services AWS has EC2 instances, Lambda functions, and Elastic Beanstalk. Azure provides Virtual Machines, Functions, and App Services. GCP offers Compute Engine, App Engine, and Cloud Functions. While all three platforms offer equivalent computing services, AWS has a much larger inventory of options, including specialized instances for specific workloads.

Difference between AWS, Azure and GCP Difference #2: Storage Services Now, if we talk about storage, AWS has S3, EBS, and Elastic File System. Azure has Blob Storage, File Storage, and Disk Storage. GCP has Cloud Storage, Cloud Datastore, and Cloud Fire store. Of these, all three provide object storage; AWS S3 is the most used and popular, with Azure Blob Storage being second and GCP Cloud Storage catching up. Difference #3: Database Services AWS has RDS, DynamoDB, and DocumentDB. Azure provides Azure Database Services, Cosmos DB, and Azure Database for PostgreSQL. GCP offers Cloud SQL, Cloud Spanner, and Cloud Firestore. While all three platforms offer relational database services, AWS has a much broader range of NoSQL database options available.

Difference between AWS, Azure and GCP Difference #4: Security and Compliance Each cloud deployment requires that a customer thinks about security and compliance. AWS has a robust security framework with IAM, KMS, and Inspector. Azure has Azure Security Center, Azure Active Directory, and Azure Policy. GCP provides a Cloud Security Command Center, Cloud IAM, and Cloud Data Loss Prevention. All three platforms provide very good security features; AWS, however, has the largest number of compliance certifications. Difference #5: Pricing and Cost Optimization One critical consideration for any cloud deployment would be pricing and cost optimization. AWS has variable pricing based on a pay-as-you-go model but offers discounts for reserved instances and committed usage. In a similar structure, Azure provides pricing on a pay-as-you-go basis with different discounts for reserved instances and Azure Hybrid Benefit. Finally, GCP offers the pay-as-you-go model with discounts applied to committed usage and sustained usage. Although all three platforms provide cost optimization features, more of the pricing options and discounts are available in AWS.

However, in 2015 we saw a global slowdown which resulted in the crunch for funding for many start-ups which resulted in many shutting shop and mass lay-offs. 5 Questions To Ask Before Joining A Startup Here are a few questions students should ask for utmost clarity to ensure they’re not signing up for a raw deal. Joining a company with a completely new idea can be risky. Many startups have failed just because they intended to deliver a product or service which had no market demand. You need to ask yourself whether the product really has the potential to go beyond fancy presentations and sell. For this, you may consider looking at its competitors and substitutes as well. How about a background check? There is nothing inappropriate to ask where the funding is coming from in order to take a peek into how well the company will be able to sustain itself. If the company is funded by venture capitalist, you will be able to know who the investors are. A background check on websites like Glassdoor and Payscale will also help you understand the internal issues faced by employees as well as the maximum pay that you can expect over a period of time.

5 Questions To Ask Before Joining A Startup There are a lot of startups which have been cloned from the Western business models. Play, parties, perks and promotions to sum it all. Getting to know who the founders are and what their visions are helps as many a time companies close down because the founders parted ways with different opinions. While some founders value the man behind the machine others treat the man like a machine! Startups have a close knit team and long working hours too. While profits are important to breakeven for a startup, people are equally important to make as well as sustain profits. So working with a startup and finishing heaps of work but having the flexibility to do it in your comfort zone on a bean bag or at home surely helps.

5 Questions To Ask Before Joining A Startup Where do you see yourself in the next five years? While the industry is changing rapidly, doing a SWOT analysis (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats) with the aid of these questions will surely help you make the right decision. AI and Machine Learning in Cyber Threat Detection. AI and Machine Learning in Cyber Threat Detection. AI and Machine Learning in Cyber Threat Detection Cyber-attacks provide a continuous and changing risk in the modern digital era. The complexity and frequency of cyberattacks have escalated as firms depend increasingly on digital platforms. Despite their continued value, traditional security measures frequently fall short in the face of these sophisticated attacks. In this context, machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) are relevant. Through faster, more precise, and more adaptable protection against cybercrime, these technologies are transforming cyber threat detection. We will examine real-world applications and the effects of AI and ML in cyber threat identification in this blog.

AI and Machine Learning in Cyber Threat Detection. Understanding AI and Machine Learning It's critical to comprehend AI and ML before delving into their cybersecurity applications. The simulation of human intelligence in machines is known as artificial intelligence or AI. Tasks like learning, problem-solving, and decision-making that normally demand human intelligence are capabilities that these systems are built for. A branch of artificial intelligence called machine learning (ML) is concerned with creating algorithms that let computers analyze and interpret data to make judgments. As ML models are exposed to more data over time, they perform better and better rather than being specifically designed for specific tasks.

AI and Machine Learning in Cyber Threat Detection. The Role of AI and ML in Cyber Threat Detection Several important techniques exist in which AI and ML improve cyber threat detection. 1 Detection of irregularities: Machine learning algorithms can examine large volumes of network data to spot trends and irregularities. Unusual login attempts or data transfers are examples of anomalies that could point to possible security risks. By looking at past data and spotting patterns, AI can forecast possible dangers. Organizations can prevent vulnerabilities from being exploited by doing this. Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered systems can react to threats automatically, cutting down on the amount of time between discovery and action. Mitigating the damage caused by cyber-attacks requires a swift response.

AI and Machine Learning in Cyber Threat Detection. AI can deliver thorough threat intelligence by processing and analyzing data from a variety of sources, such as threat databases and dark web forums. To stay up to date on the newest attack techniques and vulnerabilities, this aids security teams. Real-life Applications of AI and ML in Cyber Threat Detection A prevalent and highly destructive type of cyberattack is spear phishing. Users are tricked into disclosing personal information by cybercriminals using phishing emails and websites. Phishing attempts can be recognized and stopped by AI and ML through the analysis of email content, metadata, and user behavior.

AI and Machine Learning in Cyber Threat Detection. To identify and weed out phishing emails, for instance, Google's Gmail employs AI and ML. To better detect and flag questionable messages and shield consumers from phishing scams, the system regularly learns from millions of emails. The signature-based detection method used by traditional antivirus software is vulnerable to emerging and unidentified malware strains. Via behavior analysis and the identification of questionable patterns, AI and ML may detect malware. To detect and prevent malware assaults, for instance, cybersecurity startup Cylance employs AI. To identify malware, even if it has never been seen before, their AI-driven approach examines file properties and behavior. Protection against zero-day attacks is improved by this proactive strategy.

AI and Machine Learning in Cyber Threat Detection. Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems (IDPS) IDPS keeps an eye on network traffic to look for unusual activity or possible intrusions. These systems are made better by AI and ML, which decrease false positives and increase accuracy. For instance, the cybersecurity company Darktrace uses ML and AI in its Enterprise Immune System. This tutorial will bring you through the basic ideas of networking in clear, understandable language, with crucial topics illustrated with common instances. A network is fundamentally made up of several devices that are linked to one another to share resources and data. These gadgets, referred to as nodes, can be servers, printers, cell phones, and PCs. These devices can be connected wirelessly, using radio waves, or wired, using wires.

Overview of Network Fundamentals Consider a network as a neighborhood, for instance. The streets that connect the houses serve as the network connections, and each house stands in for a device. Devices connected to a network can interact and share resources, many ways neighbors can visit one another to exchange tools or information. 1 A Local Area Network (LAN) is a type of network that is designed to cover a limited area, like a house, workplace, or educational institution. It permits the sharing of resources, such as files and printers, and communication between devices in this vicinity. For example, A LAN is your home network. Your smartphone, laptop, smart TV, and other gadgets can all share an internet connection and communicate with one another thanks to the connections it makes.

Overview of Network Fundamentals 2 Wide Area Network (WAN): Often connecting several LANs, a WAN provides coverage over a greater geographic area. With millions of networks connected worldwide, the Internet is the greatest wide area network (WAN). For example: A business that has offices in several cities may link its office networks via a wide area network (WAN), enabling staff members to access corporate resources from anywhere in the world. 3 Personal Area Network (PAN): A PAN is a small network used for communication between personal devices, typically within a range of a few meters. For Example: When you connect your smartphone to your Bluetooth headphones, you're creating a PAN.

Overview of Network Fundamentals A router is an electronic device that routes internet traffic by forwarding data packets between computer networks. For example: Your home router routes data between your home network and the internet, making sure that requests you make to view websites are fulfilled. A switch is a device that joins devices in a local area network (LAN) and enables direct communication between them. For Example, All the computers, printers, and other devices in a small office are connected by a switch, which makes it possible for them to effectively exchange files and resources. To enable internet connectivity, a modem modulates and demodulates signals for data transfer over cable systems or phone lines.

Overview of Network Fundamentals For example, your internet service provider (ISP) usually offers a modem that transforms the signals it receives into a format that is compatible with your home network. How Data Travels in a Network Data is sent via a network in units called packets, which are smaller units of data. Each packet includes information about its destination as well as data. Before these packets get to their destination, where they are constructed again, they pass via several devices on the network. Example: Emailing someone is like mailing them a letter via the mail service. The recipient's address (destination information) is included in each envelope (packet) that contains the letter (data). The letter is assembled and read by the addressee after these envelopes pass through several post offices (network devices).

AWS Disaster Recovery Guide Step-by-Step Implementation AWS Disaster Recovery Guide Step-by-Step Implementation Disaster recovery is crucial for business continuity: In today's digital landscape, disaster recovery is crucial for ensuring business continuity and minimizing downtime. Many businesses are turning to Amazon Web Services (AWS) for their disaster recovery needs due to its flexibility, cost-effectiveness, and comprehensive suite of tools. This guide provides a systematic approach to developing a disaster recovery plan using AWS, ensuring your business is prepared for any eventuality. Disaster Recovery Definition What is Disaster Recovery?

AWS Disaster Recovery Guide Step-by-Step Implementation Disaster recovery involves strategies and processes to restore data and resume operations following a disruption, whether due to natural disasters, cyber-attacks, or system failures. Disasters can be categorized into natural events like earthquakes and floods, or manufactured issues such as hacking, system failures, and human errors. Benefits of AWS Cloud Computing platform for enabling disaster recovery of your business • AWS provides a pay-as-you-go model, reducing the need for significant upfront investments in physical hardware and allowing businesses to only pay for what they use. • Scalability- AWS's scalable infrastructure means that businesses can easily adjust their resources based on current needs, providing flexibility during disaster recovery operations.

AWS Disaster Recovery Guide Step-by-Step Implementation • Security- AWS offers robust security features, including encryption, identity, and access management, ensuring that data is always protected. Steps involved in implementing AWS disaster recovery plan for your business Step 1 Identify and Describe All of Your Infrastructure List all physical hardware components within your infrastructure. This includes servers, storage devices, and networking equipment. Document all software applications and services used, detailing versions and configurations. Map out your network architecture, including IP addresses, subnets, and connections between different components.

AWS Disaster Recovery Guide Step-by-Step Implementation Step 2 Involve the Entire Development Team Importance of Collaboration Ensure that all members of the development team are involved in the disaster recovery planning process. Their insights into dependencies and critical components are invaluable. Consider any third-party services or APIs your infrastructure relies on, such as Google Maps API, and ensure they are included in your disaster recovery plan. Step 3 Identify the Importance of Each Infrastructure Element Prioritize infrastructure elements based on their importance to business operations. Critical components should be at the top of the list.

AWS Disaster Recovery Guide Step-by-Step Implementation Assess the potential impact of losing each element. This helps in understanding which components need faster recovery times. Step 4 Discuss RTO and RPO with Stakeholders Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is the maximum acceptable amount of time to restore functions after a disruption. Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is the maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time. Balancing Needs and Costs Balance the recovery needs with the associated costs, ensuring the most critical functions are prioritized without overspending. Step 5 Cost Optimization Strategies in AWS Disaster Recovery Ensure that the instances used are appropriately sized for your needs, avoiding over-provisioning.

AWS Disaster Recovery Guide Step-by-Step Implementation For predictable workloads, consider reserved instances to benefit from lower costs compared to on-demand pricing. Implement auto-scaling to adjust resources based on demand, ensuring cost efficiency. Use lifecycle policies to move infrequently accessed data to cheaper storage classes, saving costs. Data Transfer Optimization Optimize data transfer by using services like AWS Direct Connect and methods such as compression and deduplication. Choose the right storage class for your data. Use lifecycle policies to move data to cheaper storage classes when not accessed frequently. Automate the cleanup of old backups and snapshots to avoid unnecessary storage costs.

AWS Disaster Recovery Guide Step-by-Step Implementation Step 6 Use Your Accumulated Information to Create Your Plan Leverage AWS tools like RDS for multi-AZ deployments, automated backups, and explore AWS Marketplace for custom disaster recovery solutions. Balancing Downtime and Costs Determine the trade-offs between downtime costs and recovery expenses, choosing the most suitable options for your business needs. Select appropriate backup methods, such as Amazon Machine Images (AMI) or EBS snapshots, based on your requirements. Step 7 Establish the In-House Communication Network Monitoring Responsibilities Assign responsibilities for monitoring server parameters and alerts using AWS CloudWatch and other IT infrastructure monitoring tools.

AWS Disaster Recovery Guide Step-by-Step Implementation Choosing a Monitoring Team Decide whether to reassign in-house developers for monitoring or hire a DevOps support team to handle 24/7 IT support and optimization. Step 8 Testing and Re-Testing Regularly test your disaster recovery plan to ensure it functions as expected during an actual disaster. Use AWS tools to create duplicate environments for testing real-world scenarios and validating your disaster recovery strategies. Creating a robust disaster recovery plan with AWS is essential for business continuity and minimizing downtime. By following this step-by-step guide, you can develop an efficient and cost-effective disaster recovery plan tailored to your specific needs. Regular testing and optimization will ensure that your plan remains effective and ready for any eventuality.

AWS Disaster Recovery Guide Step-by-Step Implementation What are some effective AWS DR strategies for my disaster recovery plan? AWS offers several strategies, including the Pilot Light scenario, Warm Standby, and Multi-site Deployment. Each strategy varies in complexity and cost, allowing you to choose based on your business needs. How can I optimize costs in my AWS disaster recovery plan? Optimize costs by right-sizing instances, using reserved instances for predictable workloads, implementing auto-scaling, applying lifecycle policies for storage, and automating cleanup processes. What should I include in my AWS disaster recovery plan template? An effective template should include infrastructure descriptions, team involvement, and prioritization of elements, RTO and RPO discussions, cost optimization strategies, and regular testing procedures.

AWS Disaster Recovery Guide Step-by-Step Implementation What are some best practices for disaster recovery for AWS? Best practices include regular testing, monitoring resources, setting up alerts, automating processes, and keeping detailed documentation of your disaster recovery plan. Why is it important to test a disaster recovery plan? Testing ensures that your disaster recovery plan works as expected in a real disaster, allowing you to identify and fix any issues beforehand. Blockchain Beyond Bitcoin: Real-World Applications and Innov Understanding Blockchain: The Basics In essence, blockchain is a decentralized digital journal that maintains data security and integrity by recording transactions across several computers. Peer-to-peer networks underpin blockchain operations, in contrast to traditional databases that have a central authority controlling the data. A chain is formed by the time-stamped linkage between each transaction or data entry, referred to as a block, and the previous block. The blockchain is named after this network of blocks. Key Characteristics of Blockchain 1. Decentralization: The blockchain is not governed by a single party. As a result, the data is less vulnerable to manipulation and more secure.

Blockchain Beyond Bitcoin: Real-World Applications and Innov 2. Transparency: All parties may see transactions on a public blockchain, which encourages accountability and trust. 3. Immutability: Data cannot be changed or removed once it is stored on a blockchain, guaranteeing the accuracy of the data. 4. Security: Data on blockchain is encrypted using cryptographic techniques, which greatly reduces the risk of hacking. Blockchain in Finance: Beyond Cryptocurrencies Blockchain, as a decentralized currency, was first made public by Bitcoin, but the financial industry soon realized that blockchain had far more potential. Paying money across borders is one of the most important uses. The use of intermediaries makes traditional international money transfers costly and time-consuming. Blockchain technology has the potential to expedite this procedure while lowering costs. Payments across borders can now be completed more quickly and affordably for banks and other financial organizations thanks to Ripple, a blockchain-based payment system.

Blockchain Beyond Bitcoin: Real-World Applications and Innov Moreover, smart contracts self-executing agreements with explicit language included in the code can be made using blockchain technology. Because there are fewer middlemen involved and more efficiency, these contracts automatically enforce and carry out commitments when certain requirements are met. The usage of smart contracts in diverse financial services, such as insurance and lending, has become more common thanks to platforms like Ethereum. Supply Chain Management: Blockchain Enhanced Transparency and Efficiency. Multi-party networks, ranging from manufacturers to retailers, are involved in supply chains. One of the major challenges in supply chain management is ensuring transparency and traceability. A clear and unchangeable record of every transaction and movement of commodities is what blockchain technology may offer to help with this.

Blockchain Beyond Bitcoin: Real-World Applications and Innov Walmart tracks food goods' path from farm to store, for instance, using blockchain technology. As a result, consumers' trust is increased by being transparent about the source of their food, while simultaneously ensuring food safety by promptly detecting the source of contamination. Comparably, access to a common, reliable record of data is made possible by IBM's Food Trust blockchain network, which enhances fraud prevention and traceability for different food sector stakeholders. Healthcare: Blockchain Secured Patient Data and Improving Efficiency. Inefficiencies, data silos, and security issues afflict the healthcare sector. With its safe, decentralized platform for patient data storage and sharing, blockchain technology offers promise to solve these problems. Blockchain enables patients to oversee their medical records and offers healthcare professionals access to them as needed.

Blockchain Beyond Bitcoin: Real-World Applications and Innov One such blockchain-based medical record management system is called MedRec. Data breaches are less likely because it guarantees that patient data is safe and only accessible by those who are authorized. Blockchain can also automate verifications and reduce paperwork, which helps speed up administrative tasks like billing and insurance claims. Voting Systems: Ensuring Integrity and Transparency While traditional voting systems are frequently susceptible to fraud and manipulation, elections are essential to democracy. Blockchain provides a transparent and safe election process option. Elections will be more transparent and safer if votes are recorded on a blockchain, which makes every vote unchangeable and verifiable.

Blockchain Beyond Bitcoin: Real-World Applications and Innov Blockchain-based voting methods are being investigated by several nations and organizations. For instance, West Virginia, in the United States, has tested using blockchain technology to enable military personnel to securely cast their ballots while serving overseas. Voters in remote locations or with disabilities may find voting with blockchain voting technologies more accessible. Intellectual Property: Blockchain Protects Creators’ Rights For innovators, artists, and creators, intellectual property (IP) protection is essential. It can be difficult to establish ownership and uphold intellectual property rights, though. Blockchain technology can offer a transparent and unchangeable method for managing intellectual property rights.

Blockchain Beyond Bitcoin: Real-World Applications and Innov To ensure that artists can verify ownership and trace the origin of their creations, Ascribe, for instance, employs blockchain technology to register digital art. Similar to this, the music streaming service Audius employs direct and transparent payment methods facilitated by blockchain technology to guarantee that creators are fairly compensated for their works. Real Estate: Simplifying Transactions and Reducing Fraud Fraud and inefficiency are common in the real estate sector because of the intricate transactions and copious amounts of documentation involved. Because blockchain offers a transparent and safe way to record property ownership and transfers, it can make real estate transactions easier.

Blockchain Beyond Bitcoin: Real-World Applications and Innov One platform that enables international property transfers is Propy, which is built on blockchain technology in the real estate industry. It cuts down on expenses and time by automating the whole process, from listing to contract signing. To further lower the possibility of fraud, blockchain makes a guarantee that property records are easily verifiable and unchangeable. Supply Chain of Luxury Goods: Blockchain Combat Forgery The luxury goods business suffers billion-dollar losses every year due to counterfeiting. A transparent and unchangeable record of the complete supply chain, from manufacturing to sale, is something that blockchain can offer to counteract counterfeits.

Blockchain Beyond Bitcoin: Real-World Applications and Innov To monitor the origin and legitimacy of its products, for instance, the luxury goods company LVMH created the Aura blockchain platform. By scanning a QR code, which offers a comprehensive history of the product's path through the supply chain, customers may confirm the legitimacy of their purchases. Environmental Sustainability: Blockchain Promotes Accountability and Transparency Through transparent and accountable methods for recording and verifying sustainable actions, blockchain can significantly contribute to the promotion of environmental sustainability. To make sure businesses follow through on their sustainability pledges, blockchain can be used, for example, to track a product's carbon footprint.

Blockchain Beyond Bitcoin: Real-World Applications and Innov Through the exchange of digital tokens for plastic trash, Plastic Bank, an IBM blockchain-based venture, encourages recycling. In addition to encouraging appropriate waste management and lowering plastic pollution, these tokens can be used to pay for products and services. Conclusion: The Transformative Power of Blockchain The core of Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies is not the only thing that blockchain technology is. Numerous industries, including finance, healthcare, supply chain management, and environmental sustainability, can benefit greatly from its fundamental concepts of decentralization, transparency, and immutability. Blockchain has the potential to completely change how we perform business, handle data, and engage with technology by offering safe, effective, and transparent platforms.

Blockchain Beyond Bitcoin: Real-World Applications and Innov We should anticipate seeing even more cutting-edge uses for blockchain technology as it develops to leverage its ability to solve practical issues. Comprehending blockchain technology and its various uses can lead to fascinating job prospects in a quickly expanding industry for students and young professionals. Using this technology to its full potential will improve our talents and spur positive change in global society and enterprises. Bridging the Cybersecurity Skills Gap Bridging the Cybersecurity Skills Gap Thursday, January 16, 2025 The demand for cybersecurity professionals has skyrocketed in the digital age, yet the supply of skilled individuals to fill these roles remains insufficient. The global shortage of cybersecurity experts threatens not only businesses but also governments and critical infrastructure. In this blog, we’ll explore the pivotal role higher education plays in closing the cybersecurity skills gap and building the workforce of tomorrow. The Cybersecurity Skills Gap: A Global Challenge As cyberattacks become more sophisticated and frequent, organizations require professionals equipped to handle a broad spectrum of threats, from ransomware to nation-state-sponsored attacks. Despite this pressing need, the (ISC)² Cybersecurity Workforce Study reports a workforce gap of over 3.4 million globally.

Bridging the Cybersecurity Skills Gap Several factors contribute to this gap: • The rapid evolution of technology outpaces traditional educational systems. • A lack of standardization in cybersecurity training and certifications. • Limited awareness among students about cybersecurity as a career path. Higher education institutions are uniquely positioned to address these challenges by offering specialized programs, fostering partnerships with industry leaders, and preparing students to navigate an ever-changing threat landscape. How Higher Education Can Bridge the Gap 1. Comprehensive Curriculum Development Colleges and universities can design curricula that encompass the technical and theoretical aspects of cybersecurity. Programs should cover:

Bridging the Cybersecurity Skills Gap • Cyber law and compliance By aligning course content with real-world industry requirements, educational institutions can ensure graduates are job-ready. 2. Hands-On Training and Simulations Theory alone is not sufficient in cybersecurity. Hands-on experience is critical to understanding complex concepts and developing problem-solving skills. Universities can: • Set up cyber labs where students practice penetration testing and vulnerability assessments. • Use virtual environments to simulate cyberattacks, enabling students to develop response strategies. • Encourage participation in Capture the Flag (CTF) competitions to hone skills in a gamified setting.

Bridging the Cybersecurity Skills Gap Collaboration with the private sector ensures academic programs stay relevant. Companies can provide insights into emerging trends, offer internships, and sponsor research projects. Universities can also work with industry leaders to offer co-branded certifications that add value to students' resumes. 4. Cybersecurity Bootcamps and Certifications For students and professionals looking to transition into cybersecurity, bootcamps and certification programs provide an accelerated path. Higher education institutions can offer: • Short-term courses on specific topics like cloud security or artificial intelligence in cybersecurity.

Bridging the Cybersecurity Skills Gap • Preparatory classes for certifications such as CompTIA Security+, CISSP, or CEH. 5. Encouraging Diversity in Cybersecurity The cybersecurity workforce faces not only a skills gap but also a diversity gap. Women represent just 24% of the cybersecurity workforce, according to a 2022 report by (ISC)². Higher education can lead initiatives to: • Create scholarships and mentorship programs for underrepresented groups. • Host events like hackathons to spark interest among diverse communities. • Include diversity and inclusion as core values in their cybersecurity programs. When you successfully clear your standard, or HSC, exams, it’s surely time to introspect on what you really want to take up as a career in life. It is then advisable to switch to the stream which has higher career potential after graduation and post-graduation. Career path for networking engineers after Jetking Career path for networking engineers after Jetking If you start with a solid foundation from Jetking, pursuing a career in networking engineering can be quite lucrative. The career path for a networking engineer's career is described in this blog, from entry-level jobs to more senior responsibilities, each of which calls for a unique set of abilities. 1. Trainee Network Engineer An Entry-Level Network Engineer position is the first for people just starting. To be eligible for this role, one often needs a bachelor's degree in computer engineering, information technology, or a similar discipline. To help plan, design, implement, and debug IT networks for businesses, entry-level network engineers operate as assistants to more experienced team members.

Career path for networking engineers after Jetking Knowing Internet Protocol (IP) and being able to choose the appropriate hardware for different activities are essential at this point. A strong basis in networking theory and hands-on experience with actual network settings are provided by these first duties. Furthermore, introduction to a variety of networking tools and software is common for entry-level engineers, which is essential for their development. A person can progress to become a staff-level Network Engineer after gaining experience at the entry-level. This position requires more autonomy and accountability. Among their many responsibilities is safeguarding their clients' security systems from intrusions by designing, constructing, and maintaining network infrastructure. Thorough familiarity with system software, network architecture, and all relevant configurations is required.

Career path for networking engineers after Jetking To guarantee stable and effective network performance at this point, specialists frequently need to stay current on the newest security procedures and network technology. Troubleshooting network problems, guaranteeing minimal downtime, and maximizing network performance to satisfy the demands of the company are other duties assigned to network engineers. 3. Senior Network Engineer Candidates can begin applying for Senior Network Engineer jobs after obtaining five to seven years of experience. Their technical and analytical abilities ought to have improved by now, and they ought to be well-versed in wide area networks (WANs), AWS, Azure, Cisco ASA software, IPsec, firewalls, and DNS. Lead projects, coach less experienced employees, and resolve challenging networking problems are all expected of senior network engineers.

Career path for networking engineers after Jetking High availability and security are ensured by their abilities to design and deploy cutting-edge network systems. Additionally, to ensure the smooth integration of diverse technologies and systems, senior network engineers frequently work in conjunction with other IT departments to align network strategy with overall business goals. People's job titles get increasingly specialized as they advance through the ranks. The equivalent of a network architect is a Network Engineer IV. At this level, employers are seeking professionals with experience in site surveys, network administration, security system backup, and wide and local area network (WAN and LAN) analysis for network issues.

Career path for networking engineers after Jetking Strategic planning for network improvements and expansion, performance optimization, and in-depth knowledge of network protocols are required for this position. The robustness and scalability of an organization's network infrastructure are crucially dependent on Network Engineer IVs. To maintain an up-to-date and effective network, they also assess new networking technologies and offer suggestions for their future application. 5. Principal Network Engineer The Principal Network Engineer, sometimes referred to as the Principal Systems Engineer, is the highest-level professional path in networking engineering. This position entails managing the day-to-day activities of an entire computer network. A master's degree and multiple top certifications are frequently held by candidates with this level of skill. The main network engineers are in charge of overseeing major projects, making strategic decisions, and incorporating state-of-the-art technologies into the network architecture.

Career path for networking engineers after Jetking They collaborate closely with senior management to make sure the organization's network is safe, effective, and future-proof and to match network strategy with business objectives. Principal network engineers also frequently take a key part in disaster recovery preparation and execution, guaranteeing company continuity in the event of network outages or cyberattacks. Career opportunities and Growth in networking. As more and more businesses rely on reliable network infrastructures to run their operations, there is a growing need for qualified networking experts. Industry projections predict that the demand for improved cybersecurity, cloud computing, and the proliferation of connected devices will drive a considerable expansion in the network engineer employment market over the next ten years. Due to this expansion, networking engineers have many opportunities to grow in their careers, focus on their areas of interest, and assume leadership positions within their enterprises.

Career path for networking engineers after Jetking Network engineers follow an obvious career path, where each step builds on the skills and knowledge from the one before it. Pros can begin at the bottom of the industry and work their way up to become Principal Network Engineers, which is the highest position in the business, by taking on more tasks and responsibilities as they go. With Jetking, aspirants to network engineers can start this fulfilling journey with a strong foundation and understanding. Networking engineers can accomplish substantial professional progress and make valuable contributions to their organizations by keeping up with educational advancements, gaining pertinent certifications, and improving their soft and technical abilities.

Common Methods Used by Attackers to Perform Identity Theft Common Methods Used by Attackers to Perform Identity Theft Monday, December 23, 2024 Identity theft has become a growing concern in the digital age, with attackers employing sophisticated methods to steal sensitive personal information. Understanding these tactics is crucial to safeguarding your identity and preventing financial or reputational harm. Here, we explore some of the most common methods used by attackers to perform identity theft. Phishing is one of the most widespread methods attackers use to trick individuals into revealing their personal information. This typically involves fraudulent emails, text messages, or websites that mimic legitimate entities, such as banks, government agencies, or popular online platforms. Victims are lured into providing sensitive details like passwords, credit card numbers, or Social Security numbers.

Common Methods Used by Attackers to Perform Identity Theft Example: You might receive an email that appears to be from your bank, asking you to update your account information through a link. Once you click the link, it leads to a fake website designed to capture your credentials. • Avoid clicking on suspicious links or attachments. • Verify the sender’s email address and the URL of websites. • Use two-factor authentication for your accounts. Large-scale data breaches have become a frequent source of identity theft. Cybercriminals infiltrate databases of organizations to steal vast amounts of sensitive information, including names, addresses, credit card details, and passwords.

Common Methods Used by Attackers to Perform Identity Theft Example: In a high-profile breach, attackers might compromise a retailer’s system and gain access to thousands of customers’ payment card details. • Regularly monitor your financial accounts for unauthorized transactions. • Change passwords frequently, especially after a reported breach. • Use credit monitoring services to stay alert. Skimming involves the use of devices to steal information from credit or debit card magnetic strips. These devices are often placed on ATMs, gas station pumps, or point-of-sale terminals. Example: You swipe your card at an ATM, not realizing a skimmer is installed. The device captures your card details, which attackers use to create duplicate cards or make online purchases.

Common Methods Used by Attackers to Perform Identity Theft • Inspect card readers for unusual attachments or tampering. • Use ATMs in secure and well-lit areas. • Switch to cards with EMV chips for enhanced security. Social engineering attacks exploit human psychology to gain access to sensitive information. This may involve impersonating someone you trust, such as a colleague or an IT support technician. Example: An attacker calls you, claiming to be from your company’s IT department, and asks for your login credentials to “fix” an issue. • Verify the identity of the person requesting information. • Avoid sharing sensitive details over the phone unless you initiated the contact.

Common Methods Used by Attackers to Perform Identity Theft • Educate yourself on common social engineering tactics. Malware and spyware are malicious software programs designed to steal data from infected devices. Attackers often distribute these programs through email attachments, malicious downloads, or infected websites. Example: You download a free software program that unknowingly installs spyware on your device, tracking your keystrokes and capturing sensitive information. • Install reliable antivirus software and keep it updated. • Avoid downloading software from untrusted sources. • Regularly scan your devices for malware. Although it may seem low-tech, dumpster diving remains an effective method for identity theft. Attackers search through trash to find discarded documents containing personal information, such as bank statements, medical records, or credit card offers.

Common Methods Used by Attackers to Perform Identity Theft Example: An attacker retrieves pre-approved credit card offers from your trash and uses them to open accounts in your name. • Shred sensitive documents before disposing of them. • Opt for electronic statements whenever possible. • Secure your mailbox to prevent mail theft. Shoulder surfing involves observing someone’s screen or keyboard to gather sensitive information, such as passwords or PINs. This often occurs in public places like coffee shops or airports. Example: An attacker sitting behind you in a cafe watches as you enter your email password on your laptop. • Be aware of your surroundings when entering sensitive information.

Common Methods Used by Attackers to Perform Identity Theft • Use privacy screens for your devices. • Cover the keypad when entering your PIN. Identity theft is a pervasive threat, but being aware of these common methods can help you stay vigilant and protect your personal information. Remember, safeguarding your identity is an ongoing process, and staying informed is your first line of defense.
