Quick Cybersecurity Habits You Need. Quick Cybersecurity Habits You Need. Stay Safe Online: Quick Cybersecurity Habits You Need In today's digital age, the internet is an integral part of our lives. From online banking to social media, we rely heavily on digital platforms for various activities. However, this convenience comes with risks. Cybersecurity is essential to protect our personal information and ensure our online safety. In this blog, we'll explore what cybersecurity is, and provide a set of quick habits to help you stay secure online. Cybersecurity: What is it? Cybersecurity is the discipline of protecting programs, networks, and systems from online threats. These cyberattacks frequently seek to extort money from users, access, alter, or destroy sensitive data, or interfere with regular business activities. There are more devices than people, making it difficult to implement efficient cybersecurity safeguards, and attackers are getting more creative.

Quick Cybersecurity Habits You Need. Fun Fact: The most common password is still "123456", followed closely by "password". Weak passwords are a major security risk. Why Is Cybersecurity Necessary? Cybersecurity is essential for safeguarding sensitive data and preventing illegal access to financial and personal information. It ensures the confidentiality of private conversations and actions, helps individuals and businesses avoid costly data breaches, and sustains trust by protecting an organization's brand and customer relationships. Additionally, strong cybersecurity defenses prevent service interruptions and operational disruptions.

Quick Cybersecurity Habits You Need. Quick Cybersecurity Habits You Need! 1. Use Strong, Unique Passwords The first layer of protection against online attacks is a strong password. Make sure each account has a strong, distinct password. A mix of capital and lowercase letters, digits, and special characters make up a strong password. Think about utilizing a password manager to safely keep track of your passwords. 2. Enable two-factor verification (2FA) Two-factor authentication strengthens the security of your accounts by demanding an additional form of verification in addition to your password. This can be an email verification or a code that is texted to your phone. It is far more difficult for attackers to access your accounts when 2FA is enabled.

Quick Cybersecurity Habits You Need. 3. Watch Out for Phishing Schemes Phishing schemes include sending phony emails or messages that seem official. Their goal is to steal private data, such bank account numbers or login credentials. Unwanted emails should be avoided, especially if they request private information. It is advisable to confirm the sender's identity before opening attachments or clicking on links. 4. Update your apps and software regularly Updating your software regularly is essential for safeguarding your devices from online attacks. Security patches are frequently included in software upgrades to address vulnerabilities. This holds for security software, apps, and operating systems.

Quick Cybersecurity Habits You Need. 5. Protect Your Wireless Network Cybercriminals may target your home Wi-Fi network. Modify the router's default login information, and give your Wi-Fi network a strong, one-of-a-kind password. Make sure WPA3 or WPA2 encryption is in place on your network. You may prevent data loss from hardware malfunctions or hackers by regularly backing up your data. Make use of automated backup programs and save copies of your files in several places, such the cloud and an external hard drive. 7. Make use of secure connections Make sure the websites you visit while online utilize HTTPS, which denotes a secure connection. Your internet connection can also be encrypted by using a Virtual Private Network (VPN), which adds extra protection, particularly while using public Wi-Fi networks.

Quick Cybersecurity Habits You Need. 8. Limit Personal Information Sharing Take care while sharing information online, especially on social media. Don't reveal private information such as your phone number, home address, or bank account details. You can manage who can view your posts and personal data by adjusting your privacy settings. 9. Educate Yourself and Stay Informed The field of cybersecurity is always changing. Participate in training programs, read blogs from reliable cybersecurity news sources, and stay up to date on the latest risks and best practices. Educating oneself and others can contribute to the development of a safer online community.

Rise of 5G: Transforming Connectivity and Beyond Rise of 5G: Transforming Connectivity and Beyond The arrival of 5G is among the most exciting and promising technological developments. Beyond simply delivering faster internet, next-generation wireless technology is a revolutionary development that might completely change how we work, live, and engage with the outside world. With the arrival of 5G, our lives will be impacted in every way, from enabling smarter cities to improving healthcare and encouraging industrial innovation. Here we will discuss 5G's definition, advantages, and potential impact, especially in India. Understanding 5G: A Quick Overview

Rise of 5G: Transforming Connectivity and Beyond After 4G LTE, there is now 5G, or the fifth generation of wireless technology. With it, you may connect a lot more devices at once and enjoy much quicker speeds and lower latency. Although 4G LTE can deliver up to 100 Mbps of speed, 5G is anticipated to surpass 1 Gbps, with certain networks targeting 10 Gbps. It could therefore take only a few seconds rather than several minutes to download a high-definition movie. A further significant improvement in 5G is the latency of the time it takes for a data transfer to start after an instruction. 5G seeks to cut down on 4G's latency, which is now between 30-50 milliseconds. Applications needing real-time feedback, like autonomous vehicles and remote surgeries, depend on this almost swift connectivity.

Rise of 5G: Transforming Connectivity and Beyond 5G Offers Faster Internet Speeds Fast internet speeds are among 5G's most noticeable advantages right away. Online gaming, watching HD films, and utilizing data-intensive apps will all be more pleasurable and seamless with this improvement. Can you picture having the ability to download an entire TV season in only one minute? Wow right! Comparing 5G to 4G, the former can accommodate a far higher density of devices per square kilometer. Considering the constantly increasing number of connected devices, including IoT and smartphone gadgets, this is vital. The benefits of this improved connectivity are enormous for wearables, connected autos, and smart homes.

Rise of 5G: Transforming Connectivity and Beyond New apps that need real-time communication will be made possible by 5G's lower latency. For instance, responsiveness and immersion will increase in virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) experiences. Healthcare professionals will be able to undertake precise operations from a distance because of the growing feasibility of telemedicine and remote surgeries. 5G Creates Smart Cities and Infrastructure Intelligent cities, where infrastructure is networked to increase productivity and standard of living, will be developed with the help of 5G. Congestion and pollution can be decreased by making traffic management systems more responsive. In addition to improving public services through improved data gathering and analysis, energy grids can be adjusted to control use more skillfully.

Rise of 5G: Transforming Connectivity and Beyond 2 Agriculture advances due to 5G With the use of smart agricultural technology, 5G can help India's economy, which is centered on agriculture. Drones with 5G capabilities, for example, can send rescue teams live video feeds during a flood, making it easier for them to find and help stranded people.

Routing Key Concepts for Network Administrators Routing Key Concepts for Network Administrators In the world of network management, routing plays a crucial role in directing data packets across interconnected networks to their intended destinations. Two primary types of routing exist: static routing and dynamic routing. Each has its own set of characteristics, benefits, and drawbacks. This blog will delve into the details of both static and dynamic routing, providing network administrators with the knowledge needed to make informed decisions for their network infrastructure. Static routing is a method where network traffic paths are manually configured and fixed by network administrators. In this approach, administrators manually input routes into the routing table on each router within the network, meaning the path for data traffic is predefined and does not change unless manually altered.

Routing Key Concepts for Network Administrators Key Characteristics of Static Routing: Not Suitable for Large Topologies: As the layers and complexity of the network topology increase, managing static routes becomes challenging. Since every change and configuration is done manually, maintaining a large network with static routing can be labor-intensive and prone to human error. For small and simple network topologies, static routing is easy to manage. It provides straightforward and predictable routing behavior, making it ideal for smaller networks where the traffic patterns are well-known and consistent. Manual Updates Required for Network Changes:

Routing Key Concepts for Network Administrators If any changes occur in the network, such as a topology failure, the network administrator must manually update the affected routers. This reliance on human intervention means that issues cannot be resolved automatically and require prompt action from the administrator. Static routing has less overhead compared to dynamic routing protocols because it does not require the continuous exchange of routing information between routers. This can lead to more efficient use of network resources in smaller networks. Dynamic routing, on the other hand, utilizes routing protocols that automatically exchange routing information between routers to determine the best path for network traffic. This approach adapts to changes in the network topology and can automatically update routing tables as needed.

Routing Key Concepts for Network Administrators Some Popular Dynamic Routing Protocols RIP (Routing Information Protocol): RIP is one of the oldest dynamic routing protocols. It uses a distance-vector routing algorithm to determine the best path based on the hop count. While simple to configure, RIP is not suitable for very large or complex networks due to its limitations in scalability and convergence time. OSPF (Open Shortest Path First): OSPF is a more advanced and widely used dynamic routing protocol. It uses a link-state routing algorithm to calculate the shortest path to each destination based on various metrics, including bandwidth and delay. OSPF is highly scalable and can efficiently handle large and complex network topologies.

Unlike Ethereum’s monolithic approach or Solana’s single-chain optimization, the Cosmos SDK offers horizontal scalability and modularity. Serverless Computing Simplify Infrastructure for Scalability Serverless Computing Simplify Infrastructure for Scalability Tuesday, December 24, 2024 In the rapidly evolving tech landscape, companies are constantly seeking ways to simplify their operations, reduce expenses, and scale effectively. This is where Serverless computing comes into play a revolutionary model in cloud computing that is transforming how developers build and deploy applications. " suggests a lack of servers, it actually means that developers are freed from the burden of managing server infrastructure. This shift allows businesses to concentrate on creating scalable solutions without being bogged down by intricate backend tasks.

Serverless Computing Simplify Infrastructure for Scalability What is Serverless Computing? Serverless computing is a cloud-computing model in which cloud providers like AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud dynamically allocate and manage server resources for applications. With this model, developers can write their code, upload it to the cloud, and let the platform take care of all backend processes, such as scaling, load balancing, and server maintenance. The term “serverless” does not imply that servers are nonexistent; rather, it indicates that developers do not need to oversee them. Instead, the cloud provider manages the infrastructure on-demand, allowing developers to focus solely on their applications and their functionality.

Serverless Computing Simplify Infrastructure for Scalability How Does Serverless Computing Work? In a serverless architecture, applications are divided into small units of code known as functions. These functions are executed in response to specific events, such as an HTTP request, file upload, or database update. For example, when a user uploads an image, the cloud platform triggers a function to process it, and once the task is completed, the resources are automatically released. Popular Serverless Platforms Some of the most commonly used serverless platforms include: • Microsoft Azure Functions These platforms operate on a pay-as-you-go pricing model, ensuring that businesses only pay for the actual time their code is executed.

Serverless Computing Simplify Infrastructure for Scalability Key Advantages of Serverless Computing In contrast to conventional servers in which the pre-allocated capacity is charged without considering the actual usage, serverless computing is billed only for the time (resources of the server) spent executing. This model is suitable for startups and companies that want to reduce their costs. Simplified Infrastructure Management Serverless platforms automate all backend work, including server patching, monitoring and scaling. This leads developers to be able to concentrate solely on coding optimizing. In serverless computing the scaling up or down is automatically done according to application needs. Whatever the user count, be it one, or millions, the platform guarantees that performance is only ever stable by dynamically scaling resources.

Serverless Computing Simplify Infrastructure for Scalability Speed of Development and Deployment Since much of the Operational complexity is shifted off to the cloud provider, devs can quickly build, test and deploy applications, so, serverless is something that helps agile devs. Fault tolerance and high availability are generally provided by serverless platforms and applications are able to continue operating stably even in the event of infrastructure failures. Use Cases for Serverless Computing Serverless is a great solution for small lightweight web applications (SLWAs) with little or no backend interference. Thereby the serverless functions are able to process real-time data streams, which makes these functions especially suitable for data from IoT or log files.

Serverless Computing Simplify Infrastructure for Scalability Developers can take the opportunity of serverless computing to create APIs or even divide large applications into smaller, manageable microservices. Serverless works extremely well for event-driven work, where actions for upload of files or the activities of the users are done. Using serverless, companies can develop intelligent chatbots, AI-enabled applications, etc., without the need to set up complex infrastructures. Serverless Computing Challenges The first invocation of a serverless function may not take much longer than usual as a cold start, i.e., an initialization phase. Use of services from a particular cloud provider makes platform migration afterwards challenging.

Serverless Computing Simplify Infrastructure for Scalability Because applications are distributed within serverless architecture, monitoring and debugging tend to be more challenging than local deployments. Some platforms limit the running time of a function to be executed, making this unsuitable for long running tasks. The Future of Serverless Computing Serverless computing is gaining rapid momentum across industries. Continuing progress in innovation and as competition from cloud providers pushes the boundaries, serverless computing is rapidly approaching its role as a new norm in the design of scalable, efficient applications. With this model, innovation is being driven in both very small startups and big organizations by abstracting the complexity of infrastructures, and giving developers the chance to develop innovative software.

Serverless Computing Simplify Infrastructure for Scalability Serverless computing is more than a buzzword. It represents a game-changing paradigm for developers. Because it removes the toil of infrastructure management from developers' shoulders, serverless computing enables faster development, improved scalability, and reduced cost. Companies who would like to do better at innovating and scaling could use this as a perfect chance. 1. What does “serverless” really mean? It means developers don’t need to manage server infrastructure; the cloud provider handles it for them. 2. How does serverless computing reduce costs? You only pay for the time your code runs, eliminating costs for idle server time.

Serverless Computing Simplify Infrastructure for Scalability 3. Can serverless computing handle large-scale applications? Yes, serverless platforms automatically scale based on demand, making them suitable for large-scale applications. 4. What are the limitations of serverless computing? Some challenges include cold starts, vendor lock-in, and limitations on execution time. 5. Which industries benefit the most from serverless computing? Industries like e-commerce, healthcare, finance, and tech startups leverage serverless computing for its cost-efficiency and scalability.

What are the skill development challenges in India? What are the skill development challenges in India? We had recently just held TechSparks, our annual flagship conference that saw global thought leaders, investors and the entrepreneurial community converge to discuss ideas, challenges and share their success and failure stories under one roof. This year’s conference theme ‘Tech for a Billion’, explored entrepreneurial ventures and initiatives that impacted the lives of a billion – also the kind of stories we come across at One such story I came across recently was that of Meraj Shaikh. Meraj, like many in our country, comes from a modest background, but decided to pursue a hardware technology business against all odds. Today, Miraj runs a successful business and credits his development and growth to skill development endeavours, like those of Jetking.

What are the skill development challenges in India? As its tagline suggests, Jetking aims to create a ‘Better Life’ for those with limited access to resources with its training programmes. So far, it has trained six lakh students, several of them from Tier-II and Tier-III towns and cities. I recently caught up with Siddarth Bharwani, Director of Jetking, to get his insights on the skill development space in India. Some of his shares may strike an uneasy chord with most of us: Over 20 different government bodies in India run skill development programmes but with little symbiosis. Hence, there’s an extensive duplication of work. There’s a mismatch of education and skills that young people acquire and what corporates actually require them to possess. Most of our curriculum is obsolete and lacks scope.

What are the skill development challenges in India? Accessibility for the disadvantaged and rural section of the society is difficult due to high costs involved and other social impediments. There’s a high drop rate at the age of 15 and above in many parts of India, and few skill development companies venture into those areas. There’s a dearth of engagement platforms where government organisations and industries can collaborate to make meaningful progress to curriculum and skill development. Since most companies prefer to hire candidates who already possess the right skillsets required for particular roles, more channels to propagate in-demand skills aligned with employability helps.

What are the skill development challenges in India? Experiential learning courses, i.e. a mix of classroom and practical training, can help increase retention of students. Presently, only a few institutions offer such courses in India. Skill development is not the responsibility of governments, corporates and training institutes alone; students too are equally responsible and need to recognise the changing scenario of employment. Better training and learning opportunities with the approach to holistic development (soft + technical) can help India become a truly skilled nation. India adds 12 million people to its workforce annually, but very few have any formal skill training. Today, only four per cent of the Indian workforce is skilled, in contrast to the 42 per cent in US, 76 per cent in Germany, 80 per cent in Japan and 96 per cent in South Korea. However, this could change if we reach out to more people with quality learning opportunities, revamp our existing infrastructure and execute plans more efficiently by making better use of monetary and resource support available.

We tend to train our students from a young age that “Getting Good Grades” is all that matters. The current system focuses on bookish knowledge and not enough stress is laid on practical approach to learning. This impacts the upbringing of individuals in the long run and their ability to pick up new skills themselves to carve a successful career path for themselves. The IT industry, which is set to see creation of more than four lakh jobs in the next 10 years, has now been hit by a severe crunch of manpower. The forecast says between 2012 and 2022 – 4,41,655 jobs would be created in the sector. As a part of the industry, we can point out that the gap is particularly acute in the skilled section.

Skill-Gap Wake Up Call Rapid changes in technology over the years have unfortunately not been reflected in the curriculum, which has now given rise to a skill gap. More than 50 per cent of the jobs would be in the skilled segment while demand for semi-skilled or minimally skilled jobs would be less. The industry would in fact be the second highest employment generator in the district after organized retail. Industry reports have indicated that highly skill oriented domains like data, communication and mobile would be the next drivers of the industry and the skill gap can result in the industry missing the next growth trajectory.

Skill-Gap Wake Up Call One of the major problems facing the fresh graduates is their insufficient understanding of basic concepts. The lack of in-depth understanding of hardware-related information, lack of client-handling skills and insufficient knowledge across domains are the major skill gaps in the area. While mobile computing is proving to be the next growth driver for the industry, the curriculum does not reflect it. Industry insiders say that in a strained economic condition, companies do not want to spend much on training and would prefer candidates with some skill sets who can be made billable soon. My concern is that curriculum should give idea to the students of basics of communication and other domain which will be the growth verticals of the industry. Hence we need to move in that direction which is our desired goal.

Skill-Gap Wake Up Call One of the approaches to tackle the problem of lacking job readiness in the Indian IT sector is partnerships between the industry and academia. Many multinationals have also established alliances with academic institutions on specific initiatives covering faculty upgradation, internships, curriculum revision workshops, research incubation, etc. aggregating the architects of the new global economy. IT & IMS space will form a backbone of initiatives such Digital India and Smart Cities and needs to keep pace with newer technologies with SMAC. There is also a need for innovative teaching methods, advanced courses and exceptional faculty to create globally competent IT professionals who will not only address the challenges of today but also of tomorrow.

Skill-Gap Wake Up Call India is today at a turning point and has the capability to become a World source bank for Human Resource in the future. But the country will require a skilled workforce for it take it to a global stage. India’s youth which forms a majority of the population is the advantage the country needs to leverage. The vast diversity in India, does not allow “One strategy fits all approach” when it comes to leveraging talent. A CII report on the Skill gap in India revealed that states such as Pondicherry, Rajasthan, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Harayana as compared to other states. At a city level Pondicherry, Agra, New Delhi, Coimbatore, Madurai, Chennai, Salem, Bangalore, Ghaziabad etc. fared better as compared to other cities. Hence there is also need to factor in such information while planning activities so that they are effective.

Skilling India 2.0 Somyasri Samal speaks English fluently – short, crisp sentences, grammar in place; she can also switch accents, we are told. Looking at this 22-year-old customer care executive with a telecom company, there is no way of guessing her back story. Samal is from Barundiha, 160km away from Bhubaneswar; overwhelming financial constraints at home once forced her to quit higher studies. Today, she holds a corporate job in Bhubaneswar and earns Rs 10,000 every month. “I was the first girl to step out of our village to bag a corporate job,” she says proudly. “The training in IT and communicative English helped me get the job,” she adds. She was trained at a centre run by Anudip Foundation, a Calcutta-based organisation that trains youth in market-aligned skills.

Skilling India 2.0 Samal is one among the growing number of young people in the country who have joined the skilling revolution ushered in by the central government eight years ago and Anudip is one of the 267 partner organisations of the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) under the Union ministry of skill development and enterpreneurship. “Vocational skills training is essential, especially in rural and semi-urban India. Our mantra is to make the youth a part of India’s ‘new economy’,” says Subhra Bandyapadhyaya, GM, Anudip Foundation. NSDC, along with its partners, has been able to train 8.03 million students under short-term skill courses. Says Rajiv Pratap Rudy, Union minister of state for skill development and enterpreneurship, “Out of this, 80 per cent has happened in the last two years.”

Skilling India 2.0 In its new avatar, the rejigged skilling revolution (renamed Skilling India Mission), launched last year, aims to achieve much more. The overall target is to skill 402 million workers by 2022, but the scheme now needs to connect students to real jobs – not just skill certificates. To employ the growing youth population – by 2020 half of the 1.3 billion working age Indians will be less than 25 years old – NSDC has chosen 40 sector skill councils that range from IT/ITeS to logistics, and hospitality to beauty & wellness. Says Jayant Krishna, CEO, NSDC, “We have also aligned ourselves to national missions like Make in India, Smart Cities and Digital India, mapping their requirements and thus helping in the economic development.”

Skilling India 2.0 Although the NSDC has helped train over 8 million students so far, less than half have been placed. Even the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) has questioned the way the corporation functioned till March 2014. Some partners focussed more on the number of trainees enrolled, rather than helping them land jobs. Besides, most of the jobs are limited to specific sectors, such as IT/ITeS. Take the case of Raktim Addya who was forced to cut short his higher studies after his father retired. First, he set up a tea stall and then joined Jetking Infotrain Ltd, an NSDC partner, for training in computer hardware and networking. Within a year, he landed a job in Wipro and is now earning over Rs 2 lakh per year. He says, “The certificate can help you get jobs or even start a business.”

Skilling India 2.0 Says Siddharth Bharwani, VP, Jetking Infotrain Ltd, “Such success stories point out the gaps in our conventional higher education. A majority of fresh graduates from the country’s top colleges fail to secure placements.” According to Neela Dabir, dean, Tata Institute of Social Sciences, only 20 per cent of graduates from traditional streams are employable. The rest need to acquire additional qualification to get a job. A big problem in this country is the huge mismatch between curricula and the skills required in the workplace. Says Atul Raja, executive VP of Wadhwani Foundation, a non-profit organisation that promotes skills training and entrepreneurship, “There is a marked disconnect between what academia is producing and what industry and society need.”

Skilling India 2.0 He believes this huge gap could disrupt India’s ambitious plans. “A ‘Skilled India’ is a must for Make in India. A fracture in the skills supply chain could disrupt India’s plans of manufacturing dominance (Make in India), its goals to digitally empower citizens (Digital India) or develop effective enterpreneurship (Startup India).” The major gaps in skills are in the auto industry, building and construction, textiles and retail. Aside from this, there is a skills shortage for jobs ranging from welders to masons and from electricians to nurses. InSkills, an NSDC partner, has trained a number of youths in these sectors. Says Tridibesh Bandopadhyay, co-founder and CEO, “We have placed candidates in Maruti, Larsen & Toubro and even in construction companies in Saudi Arabia.”

Skilling India 2.0 However, he rues the fact that most companies in India don’t give any preferential treatment to workers with skills training at the entry level. According to him, this discourages the youth to get trained in skills. “Many administrators also look at skilling as a poor man’s domain,” he adds. Agrees Krishna of NSDC, “We need to bring respect to skills. It’s time the youth, their parents and peers realise that no work is small.” And accept the fact that the youth needs skills that lead them to jobs. Rajiv Pratap Rudy, Union minister of state for skill development and entrepreneurship (independent charge) and parliamentary affairs

Skilling India 2.0 Q: When NSDC was launched in 2010, it set a target of educating 500 million workers by 2022. Do you think the target will be met? India had targeted to skill 500 million workers by 2022, of this NSDC was responsible for 150 million. Its target was revised to 402 million in the latest Skill India Mission and we are all geared up to achieve that goal. So far, NSDC has been able to train 80.33 lakh (8.03 million) students under the short-term skill courses. About 80 per cent of it happened in the last two years. Spanning Tree Protocol Explained: Eliminating Network Loops Spanning Tree Protocol Explained: Eliminating Network Loops Spanning Tree Protocol Explained: Making Network Loops a Thing of the Past Meet the Spanning Tree Protocol: Your Network’s Traffic Cop In the world of networking, efficiency and reliability are key. Imagine a busy metropolis where every road connects to every other road without the need for traffic signals. Chaos, right? Like this, having several paths between switches in a computer network can lead to a lot of confusion and data traffic delays. Let us introduce our story's lead character, the Spanning Tree Protocol (STP). Like how traffic signals help control the flow of cars in a city, this protocol makes sure that data moves through networks effectively and without loops.

Spanning Tree Protocol Explained: Eliminating Network Loops Why Do We Need the Spanning Tree Protocol? The Spanning Tree Protocol, or STP, is a network protocol that ensures a loop-free topology for any bridged Ethernet local area network. This means it prevents the scenario where data packets can get caught in an endless loop, endlessly circulating the network. STP was standardized by the IEEE as IEEE 802.1D. Network loops can be harmful because they can result in an overload of duplicate messages on a network, which can cause: • Broadcast Storms: Uncontrolled flooding of broadcast frames that consume all available bandwidth. • MAC Table Instability: Switches constantly update their MAC address tables with the same information, leading to incorrect forwarding of frames.

Spanning Tree Protocol Explained: Eliminating Network Loops • Multiple Frame Copies: Data frames might be received multiple times, causing confusion and potential data corruption. Spanning tree protocol helps prevent these issues by ensuring there's only one active path between two network devices, effectively eliminating the possibility of loops. Backup Paths: Always Ready, Just in Case Although loops are undesirable, redundancies can be improved by having numerous pathways, or potential loops. Spanning tree protocol can re-enable a backup path in the case when the primary link fails, guaranteeing network reliability without creating loops. How Does spanning tree protocol Work?

Spanning Tree Protocol Explained: Eliminating Network Loops The first step in Spanning tree protocol is choosing a root bridge, which is the network's core reference point. Consider the root bridge to be a company's headquarters. This root bridge is where all other switches (branches) look to determine the most effective pathways. Bridge ID: The Bridge ID is specific to each switch. The root bridge is the switch that has the lowest Bridge ID. Determining the Best Path After the root bridge is chosen, spanning tree protocol uses the cost principle to find the shortest path from each switch to the root bridge. The speed of the links determines this cost:

Spanning Tree Protocol Explained: Eliminating Network Loops Path Cost: Higher-speed lines are desired since they are less expensive. After then, spanning tree protocol keeps backup paths operational while attempting to prevent any redundant paths that might result in loops. It accomplishes this by blocking particular ports, which prevents them from forwarding data frames in favor of listening for network changes. Spanning Tree Protocol Port States • Blocking: No data is sent or received, but BPDUs are listened to. • Listening: The switch listens to BPDUs to ensure there are no loops. • Learning: The switch starts to learn MAC addresses but doesn't forward data.

Spanning Tree Protocol Explained: Eliminating Network Loops • Forwarding: The switch forwards data frames and updates the MAC table. • Disabled: The port is turned off. The Types of Spanning Tree Protocol Classic Spanning tree protocol (IEEE 802.1D) The original STP, though effective, can be slow to react to network changes. It can take up to 50 seconds to reconfigure the network after a change, such as a link failure. Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (RSTP, IEEE 802.1w) To address the slow convergence time of STP, RSTP was introduced. RSTP can reconfigure the network much faster, typically in 6 seconds or less, ensuring minimal disruption in network connectivity.

Spanning Tree Protocol Explained: Eliminating Network Loops Multiple Spanning Tree Protocol (MSTP, IEEE 802.1s) MSTP allows for multiple spanning trees to exist within a network, each covering different VLANs. This can optimize network traffic and improve efficiency by providing multiple active paths for different segments of the network. Why Should You Know About Spanning Tree Protocol? It Improves Network Reliability Understanding STP can help you design more reliable networks that can handle failures gracefully. By avoiding loops and ensuring backup paths, STP maintains network uptime and performance. Enhances Troubleshooting Skills When you know how STP works, you can more effectively troubleshoot network issues. Recognizing symptoms of loops and understanding how to resolve them can save valuable time and resources.

Spanning Tree Protocol Explained: Eliminating Network Loops Knowledge of STP is crucial for network design. It helps you create networks that are both redundant and loop-free, providing a balance between reliability and efficiency. Real-World Applications of Spanning Tree Protocol In data centers, where uptime is critical, spanning tree protocol ensures that network paths are optimized, and loops are prevented. This helps in maintaining high availability and performance. For large enterprise networks, spanning tree protocol provides a way to manage complex topologies with multiple switches and redundant paths, ensuring that data can always find its way even if some links fail.

Spanning Tree Protocol Explained: Eliminating Network Loops Campus networks, often sprawling and with multiple interconnected buildings, benefit from spanning tree protocol’s ability to prevent loops and maintain efficient data flow across different segments of the network. Although it may not be the most glamorous aspect of networking, the Spanning Tree Protocol is essential to keeping a network functional and efficient. Spanning Tree Protocol maintains consistent and reliable data flow by guarding against loops and guaranteeing redundancy. Understanding Spanning Tree Protocol is crucial whether you're building a new network, debugging an old one, or just trying to learn more about networking. You may be sure that your network will remain robust and resilient even in the event of possible outages if STP is implemented.

What Does It Take To Get IoT Jobs? What Does It Take To Get IoT Jobs? We are living in a very fast paced world. We wake up in the morning, and are in a rush to get to the office, from there we are in a rush to get home. We sleep less and focus all our energies into developing ourselves. We develop ourselves and just hope that we are working in the right direction. These ‘developers’ hone their skills with hopes of being successful in their field, without any assurance of the particular skill having a good scope in the next five to ten years. Let’s take a look at the industry, so you have a better idea what the required skills are for IoT jobs.

What Does It Take To Get IoT Jobs? Internet of Things (IoT) seems to be the hot market associated with data analytics. Anything that you can connect to the internet is essentially the Internet of Things. With international access to internet at about 3.2 billion and counting, it relates to increasing career prospects. IoT is a still developing field with additions being made on a regular basis. All the data that you see in print or the digital world, is being compiled and made meaningful by man-machine collaboration. This calls for specialization in the field of digging through the relevant data to compile a meaningful report. Hence data analytics seems to be the field with a large amount of IoT jobs scope, since people always require meaningful data to work with, in order to achieve something else.

What Does It Take To Get IoT Jobs? The added advantage for IoT jobs, is the integration of hardware and software skills. There is still a difference, but now a person working on software can develop working interest in hardware and vice-versa. Until the IoT dust settles, there is going to be a lot of such confusion as people are going to be changing roles, Contributors to the report: Dr. Milind Kulkarni, director engineering institutes, ITM group Siddarth Bharwani, vice president, Jetking Infotrain Limited Hrishikesh Kamat, chief executive officer, Shalaka Technologies pvt. ltd. According to a report by VisionMobile, “61% of wearable developers work in relatively small companies of less than 50 employees.” This comes as good news for people having doubts with regard to small organisations. Not just small organisations, “the number of developers working alone (20%) are surprisingly high.”

What Does It Take To Get IoT Jobs? Being a part of this change is very easy. The VisionMobile report also suggests the number of IoT applications developers to increase five-fold over the next five years. According to TechGig Code Gladiators – a coding contest organised by techgig.com, Java, C and C++ came up as the preferred language for programmers. Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Delhi and Mumbai were the top source of contestants. “Engineers with multidisciplinary skills are in high demand,” explains Dr. Milind Kulkarni, director engineering institutes, ITM group. According to the market, big data analytics and cloud skills are important because IoT sensors tend to send large amounts of data in real time. But the most important skills developers need, for IoT jobs, is proficiency in cloud, mobile and data analytics. Just being conversant in one skill is not enough anymore. The expertise on the trifecta would govern the salary and status with time.

What Does It Take To Get IoT Jobs? IoT requires dedicated hardware and this creates a large requirement for developers with knowledge of embedded systems. Embedded system hardware and software have to be continually updated, calling for efficient development. Development skills get you started whereas creativity would keep you going. Manufacturing hardware, adds a certain level of complexity, so as a developer, refining some of those skills in hardware, is likely to add to the skill set. This will definitely be an advantage for someone searching IoT jobs. IoT relates to connecting every device to a network. A very large number of these connections require sensors and dedicated hardware development. The current sensors include, “vibration, RF, temperature, humidity, pressure and many more” lists Hrishikesh Kamat, chief executive officer Shalaka Technologies pvt. ltd. A dedicated hardware learns from every recorded activity. “The system can learn and update after every activity,” adds Kamat.

What Does It Take To Get IoT Jobs? Automation also covers a lot of opportunities in both product and service oriented industries. According to Siddarth Bharwani, vice president, Jetking Infotrain limited, “researchers, robotics system engineers, senior robotics specialists, analysts, trainers, robotics technicians, supervisors and assistant engineers in the design and application of robot systems,” comprise the major opportunities. A lot of confusion in software Software development is an area that requires fine tuning. Decision towards a particular technology can be made fairly easily once we have a higher number of devices. According to some industry experts, C programming, JavaScript and PHP skills should be in demand. These comprise the most basic in development and hence would provide a better way to work the system.

What Does It Take To Get IoT Jobs? Some other experts believe, IoT development could see demand in Java, Android, CSS and JavaScript skills. Techgig corroborates this data w.r.t the language options. This sector is however limited to website development and management. With such a connected world, another matter of concern is security. A study by HP Fortify conducted in 2015 presented its findings, “Six out of 10 devices that provide user interfaces were vulnerable to a range of issues such as persistent XSS and weak credentials.” In a fully connected world with, “majority of the devices along with their cloud and mobile components allowed passwords such as 1234 or 123456,” security becomes a major concern.

What Does It Take To Get IoT Jobs? Additionally, higher the number of devices connected, higher the opportunities to break the system. Last year saw a rise in the number of data attacks, which were more than a hundred thousand. Bharwani adds, “Enterprises have to protect themselves, their services and their data from vulnerabilities.” Hence efficient security professionals would be in high demand. However since most of the potential weak links are similar to mobile or web applications, people currently working on security have an edge there, after all anybody would bet on an experienced horse. What’s different in development now?

What Does It Take To Get IoT Jobs? At first glance, it does not feel like much of a difference, as people are working on development and have been for more than the past couple of decades. The biggest defining factor with IoT is the ‘things’ themselves, so are the requirements in IoT jobs. Since their is no fixed device and the range of development is unlimited, coding for this broad range of devices will define IoT jobs in software development. For hardware, most of the automated devices are connected and sensor oriented. Hence incorporating sensors in every imaginable device would be the change in development. These devices ranging from a simple wearable on a personal level to dynamic street lights with warnings for over-speeding, require developers to be creative in finding solutions for specific scenarios.

What Does It Take To Get IoT Jobs? Where are the available opportunities? Metros and bigger cities are coming as target spots for job roles. “Bangalore and Pune are becoming hot locations for IT and R&D companies,” says Kulkarni. This he bases on the available talent in these places. He further explains, “Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Chennai are providing good opportunities in multiple sectors such as finance, IT and consulting.” Pune, Chennai and Sanand (Gujarat) also have major opportunities related to auto manufacturing. Opportunities will always be there in major cities as these cities provide better infrastructure along with governmental aid in business. There is however no fixed location that could provide opportunities specifically for IoT jobs and opportunities. Hardware development however would change the dynamics somewhat.

What Does It Take To Get IoT Jobs? You can’t have hardware development just about anywhere. Catering to content delivery, we have a number of data centers located in engineer efficient locations. “Large number of engineers with knowledge in automation, networking and configuring servers would also be required for setting up, maintenance and troubleshooting at the data centers,” adds Bharwani. The size and precision in IoT devices requires specific development facilities that would require setting up of heavy industries. Since such development makes more sense in commercial zones, these would be the hotbed for opportunities. The best in class opportunities can be found in places with a history of electronics manufacturing, like Silicon valley, Hong Kong, Shenzhen, Taiwan and other similar places.

What Does It Take To Get IoT Jobs? Where do you go from here? Software DIYs have become widely popular nowadays. Hence, basic application development can be picked up by spending time in front of a computer on a regular basis. IoT being the next big thing, with heavy focus on connectivity, it makes sense to update your networking skills as well. Some of the promising locations would include places with high concentrations of people looking for work with mobile development skills. So, I guess you know what to do! Technologies for Network-Based Systems in Cloud Computing Discover the key technologies driving network-based systems in cloud computing, including SDN, NFV, edge computing, AI, and more, for seamless connectivity and

Technologies for Network-Based Systems in Cloud Computing Technologies for Network-Based Systems in Cloud Computing Friday, December 06, 2024 In the dynamic world of cloud computing, network-based systems are the backbone that supports the seamless flow of data, ensuring connectivity, scalability, and efficiency. These systems rely on various cutting-edge technologies to enable businesses to thrive in an increasingly digital environment. Let’s explore the technologies that form the foundation of modern network-based systems in cloud computing. 1. Software-Defined Networking (SDN) Software-Defined Networking (SDN) revolutionizes traditional networking by separating the control plane from the data plane. This allows network administrators to programmatically manage and optimize resources, providing flexibility and efficiency. SDN is vital in cloud computing as it enables dynamic provisioning of network resources, improves scalability, and enhances security through centralized control.

Technologies for Network-Based Systems in Cloud Computing Google’s B4 SDN is a private WAN connecting its data centers worldwide. SDN helps Google optimize network bandwidth, ensuring efficient use of resources and reducing latency for services like Google Search and YouTube. 2. Network Function Virtualization (NFV) NFV replaces hardware-based network functions with software applications running on virtualized platforms. It eliminates the need for specialized hardware, making networks more agile and cost-effective. In cloud environments, NFV supports rapid deployment of services, enhances scalability, and simplifies network management, all while reducing operational costs.

Technologies for Network-Based Systems in Cloud Computing Telecom companies like AT&T use NFV to provide on-demand virtual firewalls and load balancers to customers. Instead of waiting for hardware installations, customers can scale network functions in minutes through a dashboard. Load balancing is essential for distributing network traffic evenly across servers, ensuring reliability and performance. Cloud load balancers intelligently route traffic to optimize resource utilization and prevent server overloads. They also enable high availability and scalability, which are critical for cloud-based systems handling fluctuating workloads. Amazon Web Services (AWS) Elastic Load Balancer automatically routes traffic across multiple servers in different regions. For instance, during Black Friday sales, e-commerce platforms like Shopify use this to handle surges in traffic smoothly.

Technologies for Network-Based Systems in Cloud Computing 4. Edge Computing and Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) With the rise of IoT and latency-sensitive applications, edge computing has become a vital component of cloud networking. By processing data closer to the user, edge computing reduces latency and improves performance. Complementing this, CDNs distribute content across multiple servers globally, enabling faster content delivery and improved user experiences. Netflix uses CDNs like Akamai to stream videos seamlessly worldwide. By caching popular shows closer to users, buffering is minimized. Similarly, edge computing supports smart cities by processing real-time traffic data for navigation systems like Google Maps.

Technologies for Network-Based Systems in Cloud Computing 5. Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) Security is a primary concern in cloud networking, and VPNs play a pivotal role in ensuring secure connections. By creating encrypted tunnels between devices and the cloud, VPNs safeguard sensitive data from cyber threats. This technology is particularly crucial for businesses operating in hybrid cloud environments. Businesses using cloud services like Microsoft Azure often implement VPNs for secure connections between remote employees and company resources, ensuring sensitive files are protected from hackers. 6. IPv6 and Next-Generation Internet Protocols As the demand for internet connectivity grows, IPv6 addresses the limitations of IPv4, offering a virtually unlimited number of IP addresses. Cloud networks leverage IPv6 to ensure seamless device connectivity, enhanced routing, and improved security features, paving the way for future innovations.

Technologies for Network-Based Systems in Cloud Computing Amazon Alexa and Google Home devices use IPv6 to maintain unique identities while connecting to cloud systems. The Evolution of Storage Technology in Cloud Computing The Evolution of Storage Technology in Cloud Computing Monday, December 16, 2024 Cloud computing has reshaped how data is stored, accessed, and managed. Behind this transformation is the remarkable evolution of storage technology. From rudimentary beginnings to sophisticated systems capable of handling zettabytes of data, storage in the cloud has undergone a journey of innovation. From bulky physical systems to intelligent, distributed networks, the progression of cloud storage is a story of innovation and adaptability. Let’s delve into this evolution and understand how storage technology in the cloud has transformed over time. Let's explore this evolution.

The Evolution of Storage Technology in Cloud Computing The Dawn of Data Storage: The 1960s to 1980s The earliest forms of data storage were local and physical. Punch cards, magnetic tapes, and later floppy disks provided rudimentary storage solutions. These mediums were fragile, had limited capacity, and required physical access to retrieve data. As businesses expanded, the need for centralized storage solutions emerged. Networked storage, such as Network Attached Storage (NAS) and Storage Area Networks (SAN), marked the first steps toward scalable, accessible data systems. The Rise of Virtualization: The 1990s The 1990s introduced a groundbreaking concept: virtualization. This allowed physical storage to be abstracted into virtual units, enabling better utilization and scalability. Storage virtualization became the backbone for early cloud services like file hosting and sharing.

The Evolution of Storage Technology in Cloud Computing The decade also saw the rise of Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID), which improved reliability by distributing data across multiple drives. Cloud Storage is Born: The 2000s With the advent of high-speed internet, cloud computing began to take shape. Amazon Web Services (AWS) launched S3 (Simple Storage Service) in 2006, offering businesses scalable, on-demand storage. – Storage could expand or shrink as per demand. – Pay-as-you-go models reduced upfront costs. – Data could be accessed from anywhere with an internet connection. During this period, advancements in distributed systems allowed data to be stored across multiple data centers, ensuring high availability and disaster recovery.

The Evolution of Storage Technology in Cloud Computing The Era of Intelligent Storage: The 2010s As cloud adoption surged, storage technology became more intelligent. Tiered storage was introduced, where data was automatically moved between high-speed and cost-efficient storage tiers based on usage patterns. Key developments included: Ideal for unstructured data like images and videos. Hybrid Storage Solutions: Combining on-premise and cloud systems for flexibility. Abstracting storage management, focusing on data interaction. Encryption and advanced security protocols became standard to address growing concerns about data privacy and breaches. Modern Cloud Storage: 2020s and Beyond

The Evolution of Storage Technology in Cloud Computing Today, storage technologies are defined by speed, intelligence, and eco-friendliness. NVMe (Non-Volatile Memory Express) and SSDs (Solid-State Drives) provide lightning-fast access. AI and ML are transforming storage management: • Predictive analytics optimize storage utilization. • AI-powered recovery systems ensure data is never truly lost. Decentralized cloud storage solutions, leveraging blockchain, are emerging, offering enhanced security and transparency. The push for sustainable cloud practices has also led to the rise of energy-efficient data centers. The Future of Cloud Storage Looking ahead, storage technology will likely become:

The Evolution of Storage Technology in Cloud Computing Leveraging quantum computing for unparalleled processing and storage capabilities. Storing data closer to its source for real-time applications. AI-driven systems that can autonomously resolve issues. Cloud computing has redefined how we interact with data, and its evolution is a testament to human ingenuity. From modest beginnings to cutting-edge solutions, the journey of storage technology continues to inspire and transform our digital landscape. Explore the latest advancements in cloud storage and discover how they can revolutionize your business today!

Top 10 Cloud Computing Trends in 2024 Top 10 Cloud Computing Trends in 2024 As we move into 2024, cloud computing is a vibrant and exciting driver of innovation and opportunity. Top 10 Cloud Computing Trends in 2024 1. AI and ML: Rise of AI-as-a-Service Cloud infrastructure, in democratizing AI to the masses, will play a huge role in delivering the associated economic and social benefits expected from it. AI models the LLM behind ChatGPT is one of those models that are trained on vast amounts of data using vast computing. With AI as a Service, businesses can harness the transformational power of AI without the constraints of resource management. 2. Data Security: A Growing Concern Data thefts and breaches are spiraling in incidence and impact as hackers dream up new AI-powered forms of attack. Security and resilience will be therefore uppermost in the minds of all cloud providers and customers. The three cloud computing service functions that will gain the most in-demand through 2024, facing the evolving threat landscape, are encryption, authentication, and disaster recovery.

Top 10 Cloud Computing Trends in 2024 3. Multi and Hybrid Cloud Deployment: Flexibility in a Different Light. The proportion of large organizations having a multi-cloud strategy, wherein they buy services from more than one provider, is said to grow from 76% to 85% throughout 2024. Multi and hybrid cloud, mixing cloud with on-premises infrastructure, are sophisticated infrastructure solutions that will continue to widen their footprint as organizations balance security with flexibility and cherry-pick the services they need. 4. Low Code and No Code Cloud: Democratization of Cloud Services Low-code/no-code tools enable people to build applications that otherwise would need trained software engineers. Cloud service providers can use drag-and-drop interfaces and natural language tools to eliminate the need for advanced technical skills in a bid to "democratize" the deployment and management of cloud services and infrastructure.

Top 10 Cloud Computing Trends in 2024 5. Sustainable Cloud Computing: A New Era of Environmental Responsibility The big cloud service providers all claim to be well on the way to achieving net zero able to cancel out all the carbon their operations have used up, and some of those providers are even becoming part of the solution. To Green Computing is an umbrella of environmentally sensitive practices involving computers, and chips tech of many varieties—from design and manufacturing, through use and disposal. 6. Serverless Computing: The New Model for Cloud Computing Serverless computing is a model in which the need for the management of servers is eliminated for businesses. While in a regular cloud service, the business would be charged by the number of servers they want to host their infrastructure on, in the case of a serverless model, they only pay for resources used directly.

Top 10 Cloud Computing Trends in 2024 7. Edge Computing Everywhere: A New Era of Real-Time Processing Edge computing is the process whereby information of cloud computing-related paradigms is processed closer to the source from where it is collected. For example, a wearable real-time heart monitor could be designed to pick up arrhythmias. 8. Real-Time Cloud Infrastructure: A New Era of Instant Insight In 2024, this will shift to a greater interest in how to use real-time data to gain insight minute by minute, rather than acting on information that's hours or even days old. At the same time, a growing proportion of the data we ingest will be in the form of streamed data: movies and music from Netflix and Spotify, video data from Zoom or Teams calls, and new forms of streamed entertainment like cloud gaming.

Top 10 Cloud Computing Trends in 2024 9. Cloud-driven innovation and transformation—a new era of possibility Besides AI, above, utilizing cloud computing technology can be the way to a whole stack of different transformative technologies, including IoT, blockchain, and quantum computing. 10. Cloud privacy: A growing concern Cloud privacy refers to the technological, regulatory, and legislative solutions that will continue to help businesses leverage cloud while customers can be assured that their data is fully protected. Normally, using a cloud service is tantamount to transferring data to a third party, usually, the cloud service provider, which then becomes a challenge in managing the associated privacy implications a theme expected to assume center stage in cloud computing in 2024.

Top 10 Difference in iPhone and Android in 2026 What is the difference between iPhone and Android? The main difference between iPhone and Android is their operating system. iPhones run on iOS by Apple, while Android phones use Google’s Android OS. iOS offers a smooth, secure, and closed ecosystem, whereas Android provides customization, wider device choices, and flexible pricing. Which is better: iPhone or Android? iPhone is better for users who want strong security, smooth performance, long software updates, and a premium ecosystem. Android is better for users who want customization, more phone choices, lower prices, and expandable features.

Top 10 Difference in iPhone and Android in 2026 Is iPhone an Android phone? No. iPhone is not an Android phone. iPhones use Apple’s iOS operating system, while Android phones use Google’s Android OS. iOS is Apple’s mobile operating system used only in iPhones, while Android is Google’s operating system used by brands like Samsung, OnePlus, Xiaomi, and others. The most significant difference lies in their operating systems. iPhones run on Apple’s iOS, known for its smooth performance and user-friendly interface. In contrast, Android devices utilize the Android operating system developed by Google, offering more customization options. Android is celebrated for its high level of customization. Users can modify the home screen layout, install custom launchers, and change the overall look of their devices. On the other hand, iOS maintains a more uniform design, focusing on simplicity and ease of use with limited personalization options.

Top 10 Difference in iPhone and Android in 2026 Each one platform boasts its own app store. iPhones access the Apple App Store, while Android devices use the Google Play Store. Although both stores offer a vast selection of apps, the Apple App Store is often viewed as more curated and secure. Android, however, allows users to download apps from third-party sources, providing greater variety. Why iOS is better than Android Android’s open-source nature means multiple manufacturers produce Android devices, resulting in a wide range of choices in hardware, designs, and price points. In contrast, iPhones are exclusively manufactured by Apple, leading to fewer options but ensuring consistent quality and performance.

Top 10 Difference in iPhone and Android in 2026 Android caters to a broader audience with devices available across various price points, from budget-friendly options to high-end flagship models. iPhones generally come with a higher price tag and fewer budget options, making Android a more accessible choice for many consumers. iOS typically offers a straightforward and intuitive user interface, making it easier for newcomers to navigate. While iPhones provide a consistent experience across devices, Android can vary significantly depending on the manufacturer. Some Android devices come with heavy customizations, which can be confusing for some users.

Top 10 Difference in iPhone and Android in 2026 Apple is renowned for its timely software updates. When a new iOS version is released, it’s available for all compatible devices almost immediately, ensuring users receive the latest features and security updates. Conversely, Android updates can vary by manufacturer and carrier, resulting in delays or even a lack of updates for some devices. Apple places a strong emphasis on user privacy and security, with features like Face ID and end-to-end encryption for iMessages. While Android devices also prioritize security, they have faced more issues with malware and breaches due to the platform’s open-source nature. Nevertheless, both platforms offer robust security features, and users should practice safe browsing habits.

Top 10 Difference in iPhone and Android in 2026 Integration with Other Devices For users with multiple Apple products, such as a MacBook or Apple Watch, the integration is seamless. Features like Handoff and AirDrop facilitate easy file sharing and task continuation across devices. While Android integrates well with Google services, it lacks the same level of compatibility with hardware from other manufacturers. Apple is known for its excellent customer support. Users can visit Apple Stores for in-person assistance, making it easier to resolve issues. Android support, however, varies by manufacturer, some offer outstanding support while others may fall short. This discrepancy can be crucial for users who prioritize customer service.

Top 10 Difference in iPhone and Android in 2026 Choosing between an iPhone and an Android device ultimately comes down to personal preference and priorities. If you value customization, a broader range of hardware options, and budget-friendly choices, Android may be the better option. Conversely, if you prefer a streamlined experience, regular software updates, and strong integration with other devices, an iPhone could be the way to go. Both platforms have their strengths and weaknesses, so consider which features matter most to you before making a decision. Regardless of your choice, both offer impressive capabilities to cater to a variety of user needs.

As the world shifts towards more connected devices, understanding these differences becomes crucial. IPv4, or Internet Protocol version 4, was the first version of IP developed for public use. Introduced in 1981 by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA), it became a production standard on SATNET and ARPANET by January 1983. IPv4 addresses are 32-bit numbers represented in decimal format. These addresses are divided into four octets separated by dots, with each number ranging from 0 to 255. For example, an IPv4 address might look like 192.168.1.1.

These addresses consist of eight groups of four hexadecimal digits, separated by colons, like 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334. Defining the negation of these two hacker types is critical for such organizations and individuals seeking to safeguard their digital being. What is White Hat Hacking? White Hat Hacking is an authorized hacking (ie, hacking with permission) in which the hacking is permissible by system owner. Ethical hackers, or the hackers of choice, operate as the advisors of cyberattacks for taking an approach that helps companies to discover and repair weaknesses within their systems. For example, they are playing a key role in the cybersecurity development process and companies and governments use them.

Top Difference between White Hat and Black Hat Hacking Key Characteristics of White Hat Hackers: They work with permission from the system’s owner. The aim is to improve system security and protect personal data. Penetration testing is performed by so-called ethical hackers, and it is strictly regulated according to a predefined set of rules and a toolkit. There are many professional certified as CEH ( ), CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional) or OSCP (Offensive Security Certified Professional). What is Black Hat Hacking? Black Hat Ha0king is a type of crime in which, intentionally, hackers exploit system vulnerabilities, the nature and the owner of the system knows extent of which. These attackers are engaged in malicious activity, such as data exfiltration, malware spreading and system disruptiveness for pecuniary gains or simply for entertainment.

Top Difference between White Hat and Black Hat Hacking Key Characteristics of Black Hat Hackers: They break into systems without the owner’s consent. Their end aim is destructing or stealing information or to disrupt, systems. Engage in schemes for phishing, ransomware, and identity theft. Black box hackers rarely operate openly, as they tend to stay under the radar, there for law enforcement. Why Understanding These Differences Matters There is a need to assess the difference between white hat and black hat hacking to promote cybersecurity. Organizations can be made more secure by engaging ethical hackers to identify weaknesses prior to exploitation. Conversely, knowledge of the techniques employed by attack scenarios that are perpetrated through black hat hackers can be used to develop practical countermeasures for preventing attack.

Top Difference between White Hat and Black Hat Hacking Interestingly, despite white hat hackers and black hat hackers possess the same technical skill; they have different aims and methods. In cybersecurity, white hat hackers, taking advantage of security flaws and privileges within the legal framework, aim to make applications more secure, in contrast with black hat hackers who take advantage of such security flaws for their own benefit and act unethically. Types of hackers in the industry Hackers range from ethical White Hats to malicious Black Hats, with Grey Hats, Script Kiddies, Hacktivists, APTs, and Cyber Mercenaries in between.

Types of hackers in the industry Types of hackers in the industry Exploring the various types of Hackers in the current industry Hackers play a crucial but frequently misunderstood role in the fast-paced field of cybersecurity. They represent a range of abilities, motives, and moral standards; they are not merely evil holders hiding in the shadows. Knowing the various kinds of hackers will help you better understand their varying types and the steps that must be taken to effectively counter cyber threats. 1. White Hat Hackers (Ethical hackers) Cybersecurity enthusiasts or white hat hackers are the real heroes. They test and enhance network, applications, and systems security, using their expertise. White hats, who diagnose and address vulnerabilities before malevolent hackers do, are frequently hired by companies or function as independent consultants. They perform penetration testing sometimes known as “pen testing” and vulnerability assessments. Boosting defenses and preventing cyberattacks are their main objectives.

Types of hackers in the industry As opposed to white hackers, black hat hackers commit crimes, for malicious reasons or personal benefit. They leverage system weaknesses to steal information, scam people or disrupt operations. A lot of times these hackers are linked to illegal actions like ransomware attacks, financial fraud, and identity theft. Black hat hackers may cause an immersive amount of harm to people and identity theft. Between white hat hackers and black hat hackers are the morally grey area where grey hat hackers operate. They might find security holes without authorization, but they’ll still report them to the impacted company sometimes even demanding payment in return for the information. Grey Hats operate outside the law and may still be prosecuted for unapproved hacking activity, even though their intentions aren't always malicious.

Types of hackers in the industry When launching attacks, script kiddies use pre-written programs or tools rather than the technical expertise of seasoned hackers. They frequently aim at well-known weaknesses without completely grasping the workings of their methods. Rather than being driven by money, script kiddies are usually driven by desire to exploit others or demonstrate their hacking abilities. These hackers are not as skilled as others, yet they can still cause system disruptions and data compromises. In Hacktivism, hackers utilize their expertise to further political or social objectives combining the best elements of activism with hacking. They aim at businesses, governments, and other organizations that they consider to be oppressive or immoral. Data breaches meant to reveal private information are among the hacktivist tactics, as are defacements and DDoS (Distributed denial of service) operations. Hacktivism can be motivated by a wide range of issues, such as defending free speech, opposing human rights violations, or environmental policy.

Types of hackers in the industry 6. State-Sponsored Hackers (APT Groups) Advanced Persistent Threat groups, commonly referred to as state-sponsored hackers. Work on behalf of the government or other state institutions. Typically, they aim to disrupt other governments, and infrastructure, obtain intelligence or engage in spying. APT groups are highly skilled breaking into targeted systems with cutting edge methods and zero-day exploits (vulnerabilities that the public is unaware of) With an eye toward long-term strategic advantages, their operations may last for months or even years. In the domain of technology. Cyber Mercenaries are hired experts who will hack anything for anyone who will pay them. To perform cyber spying undermine rivals or initiate cyber-attacks on behalf of their clients, they might work for businesses, criminal groups, or even governments. The primary incentive for cyber mercenaries is money; they are motivated by contrast that offers large salaries and significant compensation for their hacking skills.

Types of hackers in the industry In cybersecurity exercises and organizations, the terms “blue team” and “red team” are for defensive and offensive cybersecurity teams. Security measure implementation, incident response, and network and system defenses are the main focuses of blue teams. By stimulating assaults and discovering vulnerabilities that require mitigation, red teams act as attackers assessing how well blue team defenses are working. This corporative strategy aids in enhancing an organization’s overall cybersecurity posture. In the cyber security space, hackers come in many forms. From morally responsible professionals protecting digital networks to malevolent individuals causing chaos for their own benefit or political convictions, the scene is complicated and varied. To build strong cybersecurity tactics and keep one step ahead of emerging threats, it is essential to comprehend the motives and techniques of various hacker types. Businesses may strengthen their defenses and reduce the risk posed by malevolent hackers by utilizing ethical hacking techniques, guaranteeing a safer digital future for everybody.

Understanding Rootkit will patch, hook, or replace the versi Understanding Rootkit will patch, hook, or replace the versi How rootkits patch, hook, or replace system calls to hide information Friday, December 27, 2024 Learn how rootkits patch, hook, or replace system calls to hide information, evade detection, and manipulate OS behavior. Stay informed and secure your systems. In the world of cybersecurity, rootkits represent a particularly insidious class of malware designed to provide unauthorized access to a computer system while remaining hidden from detection. Among the various types of rootkits, stand out for their ability to manipulate the system's core functions. These rootkits often patch, hook, or replace system calls to conceal their presence and hide malicious activity, making them a formidable challenge for security professionals.

Understanding Rootkit will patch, hook, or replace the versi When it comes to stealthy and dangerous malware, rootkits are among the most feared. A particular type of rootkit that excels in hiding information and activities from users and security tools is one that targets system calls—the fundamental mechanism through which applications interact with the operating system. This type of rootkit, known as a kernel-mode rootkit, manipulates the system at its core, modifying the behavior of system calls to conceal its presence and malicious operations. System calls are interfaces provided by the operating system to enable user-level applications to request services such as file operations, memory management, and process control. For example, when you list files in a directory, your application sends a system call to the kernel to retrieve that information.

Understanding Rootkit will patch, hook, or replace the versi Kernel-mode rootkits exploit this process by intercepting and altering these system calls. By doing so, they can manipulate the results returned to the user or other applications, effectively hiding their tracks. How Do Kernel-Mode Rootkits Manipulate System Calls? Kernel-mode rootkits use three primary techniques to interfere with system calls: • The rootkit modifies the system call table, replacing legitimate entries with its own malicious functions. For instance, the system call responsible for listing files in a directory could be patched to exclude certain files, such as those associated with the rootkit.

Understanding Rootkit will patch, hook, or replace the versi • This approach allows the rootkit to alter the output of the operating system at a fundamental level, hiding files, processes, or network connections. • Instead of directly modifying the system call table, hooking involves redirecting the execution flow of a system call to a custom function before or after the legitimate function is executed. • Hooking provides flexibility, enabling the rootkit to filter or modify data dynamically. For example, a hooked system call for process enumeration could skip over processes associated with the rootkit. • Some kernel-mode rootkits go a step further by replacing legitimate kernel modules or injecting their code into the kernel. This allows them to intercept and manipulate system calls as if they were part of the operating system’s core functionality.

Understanding Rootkit will patch, hook, or replace the versi • Such rootkits can remain deeply embedded and persistent, making them extremely difficult to detect or remove. Why Is This Technique Used? The primary purpose of manipulating system calls is to hide malicious activity. By altering the results of operations such as file listing, process enumeration, or network monitoring, kernel-mode rootkits can: • Hide files or directories containing their malicious payloads. • Conceal processes running in the background to carry out attacks. • Mask network connections used for data exfiltration or communication with command-and-control servers. The Danger of System Call Manipulation

Understanding Rootkit will patch, hook, or replace the versi Kernel-mode rootkits operate at the most privileged level of the operating system, which makes them incredibly powerful. This level of access allows them to bypass standard security measures and remain hidden from most user-mode monitoring tools. Additionally, their ability to manipulate core system operations makes them a potent threat. Rootkits that patch, hook, or replace system calls are among the most sophisticated tools in a cybercriminal’s arsenal. Their ability to seamlessly integrate into the kernel and manipulate critical OS functions makes them difficult to detect and even harder to remove. Understanding how these rootkits operate is crucial for developing robust defenses, as well as for recognizing the signs of their presence in a compromised system.
